(1) MARK FRESHNESS: the pre-open runs were right to flag their marks stale, and this run cleared both flags with live quotes -- the handoff pattern worked and should be repeated whenever a run fires before 09:30 ET. That is legitimately realized volatility, but it biases iv_rv_ratio LOW -- i.e. makes premium look CHEAP -- for any name that recently reported. MSFT's 0.53 and TSLA's 0.59 should NOT be read as 'cheap premium, buy single-legs' without checking whether an earnings gap is doing the work. substantive_finding.headline: FIRST post-midnight-UTC run in this automation's history -- and 'today' is dangerously ambiguous at that boundary. Three per-day artifacts would have been silently corrupted by rolling them on the UTC date. Root fix written to CLAUDE.md.
substantive_finding.how_it_surfaced: This run fired at 2026-08-14T00:45Z, i.e. 19:45 ET on THURSDAY 2026-08-13. Every prior post-close run landed before 00:00 UTC (20:28Z, 21:30Z, 22:33Z, 23:29Z), so no instance had ever faced the boundary. By UTC date, this run IS 'the first run of 2026-08-14'. By trading calendar, Friday has not begun and will not for another ~9h45m.
artifacts_at_risk: automation_heartbeat.json (dated 2026-08-13, stamped 13:05Z by that day's first run): stamping it '2026-08-14' now would PRE-SATISFY the dead-man alarm for a trading day that has not started. If the cron then died overnight, Friday would look healthy all day and the single alarm designed to catch a dead automation would never fire. This is the most dangerous of the three -- it disables a safety mechanism rather than merely producing bad data.

market_brief.json (date 2026-08-13, built 13:08Z pre-open): the run prompt says 'If market_brief.json isn't stamped today, build it.' Read on the UTC date, that instruction fires RIGHT NOW -- and a brief built at 00:45Z off overnight/thin extended-hours prints would then be stamped 2026-08-14, so Friday's genuine pre-open and first post-open runs would see it 'already stamped today' and SKIP the rebuild. Friday would be traded off Thursday-night quotes.

The -$200 realized daily loss cap and the 'max 3 new entries per day' throttle: both reset on the trading day. A UTC rollover does not hand the desk a fresh loss cap or a fresh entry budget -- and reading it that way would mean a bad Thursday could be followed by full risk appetite at 19:46 ET the same evening.
substantive_finding.action_taken: DECLINED to stamp the heartbeat, DECLINED to rebuild the brief, and treated the loss cap / entry throttle as still belonging to the 2026-08-13 session. Then made the durable fix: added a new bullet to the CLAUDE.md options-automation ruleset -- "'Today' means the US TRADING day (ET), never the UTC calendar date" -- enumerating all three artifacts and stating the rule that on any run between the 16:00 ET bell and the next 09:30 ET open, the trading day is still the day whose bell just rang. Reconcile, log, stand down; roll nothing forward. Per the standing 'fix issues at the root' principle, the next instance inherits the answer instead of re-deriving it at 00:45Z under time pressure.
substantive_finding.not_a_trading_signal: This changes no position, no size, no thesis and no risk number. It is a process defect in the run-scaffolding, caught before it cost anything.

That is a real gate doing real work, and no run this week complied-by-accident: one run noted the problem in passing ('any new entry would itself be an override requiring a written argument'), correctly, and still declined on the merits. THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.the_tension_for_RYAN_to_resolve: This looks like an unintended interaction between two rules written at different times, not a mistake by any instance. On 2026-08-05 Ryan RAISED the options budget to $1,500 precisely so the sleeve could size up on quality ('as long as the trades are quality thought out it can use up to 1500'), and authorized the hedge in the same breath. The run prompt's ~$750 soft cap on total deployed premium was written separately. Together they mean the Ryan-authorized hedge alone exhausts the soft cap, leaving the sleeve able to use only $1 of the $1,500 he approved without logging an override every time. Two coherent readings, and an agent may not pick between them: (a) the ~$750 is meant as a cap on NON-HEDGE deployed premium, in which case $751 of headroom is live and the freeze is purely opportunity-set; or (b) the ~$750 is meant as a genuine total-book ceiling, in which case the sleeve is intentionally near-frozen while the hedge is on and that should be stated so instances stop treating it as a live budget.
THE_REAL_FINDING_STRUCTURAL_NOT_DRIFT.explicitly_NOT_a_recommendation_to_loose: No unattended run may loosen a gate, and this run did not and does not propose to. Nothing here was overridden, no entry was taken, and the correct behavior in the meantime is unchanged: if a genuine A+ setup appears, write the two-sentence override argument BEFORE acting, exactly as the prompt requires. ON THE CHEAP-VOL OBJECTION: it is weaker than the prior run assumed. Within this expiry the skew RISES with strike (105C 67.90% < 115C 69.27% < 120C 70.50% IV), so a call debit spread sells a HIGHER IV than it buys -- it is not simply 'short cheap vol'. The genuine argument against the spread is different and still stands: INTC's realized vol (80%) exceeds implied (68%), meaning the stock tends to travel further than the options price, which is exactly when a capped payoff costs you most on a breakout thesis. RECOMMENDATION TO THE NEXT RUN, offered as analysis and NOT as authorization: if INTC triggers, the 2026-09-18 120C at ~$450 satisfies every constraint at once -- budget fit with room, best liquidity on the chain, right delta, long vol.

structural_finding.headline: THE AGENTIC ACCOUNT CANNOT TRADE DEBIT SPREADS. It is option_level_2; spreads require option_level_3. This is the most important thing this run produced and it is not a market observation -- it is a permanent capability limit that has been silently shaping every vehicle decision this desk has made.
structural_finding.how_it_was_found: Honestly: by accident, while trying to rescue a trade. The 16:15Z run killed AVGO -- the best candidate of the day -- on VEHICLE ECONOMICS alone, after overturning two of the four reasons the run before it had used. Its stated disqualifier was that the only earnings-clean expiry (2026-08-21, 7 DTE) bleeds ~6.8% of premium per day with a weekend to pay. The obvious repair is the desk's OWN standing preference -- 'Prefer debit spreads over single-legs at this account size' -- which nobody had actually priced today. I priced it, and then checked whether it could be executed. It cannot.
structural_finding.the_evidence: get_accounts returns option_level='option_level_2' for 718757339. The connector's own get_option_level_upgrade_info documentation states it plainly: 'option_level_2 enables long calls/puts, covered calls, and cash-secured puts; option_level_3 adds spreads and complex strategies.' Ryan's separate individual account 5ST95513 carries option_level_3 -- so the agentic account's level 2 is a per-account setting, not an account-holder limitation, which is why the approval is plausible if he applies.
structural_finding.why_it_is_dangerous_and_not_academic: This is the part a future instance must not miss. The routine prompt authorizes debit spreads 'legged ONE order at a time: long leg in first, short leg out first.' On an option_level_2 account that sequence FAILS UNSAFELY, not cleanly: the long leg FILLS, and the short leg is then REJECTED for insufficient options level. The sleeve is left holding an unintended, full-premium, naked single-leg it never decided to own -- at up to the $1,500 per-trade maximum -- with the theta profile it had specifically chosen a spread to AVOID. A run that reaches for a spread without checking the level first does not get a failed order; it gets a position. CHECK option_level BEFORE SENDING LEG ONE.
structural_finding.what_it_has_cost: Measurable, and worth stating so the upgrade case is made on numbers rather than on feel. I priced the AVGO 2026-08-28 board (14 DTE, earnings-clean, spot 394.825) live at 16:31:51Z. Single legs: 395C mid $12.85 (spread 7.78% of mid, theta -3.67%/day, but $1,285 = 86% of the per-trade max on OI 109); 410C mid $6.98 (9.31%, -6.17%/day); 420C mid $4.375 (8.00%, -8.31%/day). The corresponding VERTICALS, at mid: 395/415 debit $735, net theta -1.02%/day, BE +1.91%; 395/410 debit $587, net theta -0.70%/day, BE +1.53%; 400/420 debit $607.50, max profit $1,392.50, net theta -1.62%/day. So the structure the desk is told to prefer would have cut carry from roughly -6.8%/day to -0.7-1.6%/day -- a 4-9x improvement in exactly the variable that has now killed the day's best candidate twice -- while also HALVING the capital at risk versus the $1,285 ATM single leg. That is the cost of the missing permission, quantified.
structural_finding.what_i_did_not_do: I did not treat this discovery as a reason to trade. Finding a better vehicle does not upgrade a B setup, and 'I finally solved the structure problem, so let us use it' is precisely the momentum-toward-a-trade the mandate warns about -- the same trap the 16:15Z run flagged in itself an hour ago. AVGO fails on THESIS before it ever reaches the vehicle question (see below). The spread work is recorded as a capability finding for future setups, not as a justification for this one.

It is recorded and then OVERRULED: the level was written without an index-relative escape clause, twelve consecutive 5-min closes failed to take the trigger out, and the whole function of a pre-written level is that it is not re-argued at the moment honoring it costs something. The desk's rule -- 'the level does not move down to meet the tape' -- applies identically to a kill level moving UP to spare a candidate.

process_finding_worth_keeping.title: The iv_rv_ratio systematically lies for ~30 sessions after an earnings print, and it lies in the direction that invites bad trades.
process_finding_worth_keeping.measurement: Dropping the two largest absolute daily moves from each 30-session window: SPY 1.06->1.23, QQQ 0.89->1.10, NVDA 1.03->1.14, AMD 0.71->0.84, TSM 0.89->1.26, AVGO 1.12->1.34, MSFT 0.52->1.01, TSLA 0.72->1.24, RBRK 1.20->1.40. Six of nine flipped from 'cheap' to 'fair-to-rich'; only AMD stayed below 1.0.
process_finding_worth_keeping.why_it_matters: rv_30d is a 30-SAMPLE stdev, so one gap dominates it. Every core name printed earnings inside the current window. The desk's standing preference is to prefer IV/RV below 1.5 where history is thin -- which means the mechanical number has been quietly green-lighting premium that is not cheap.
process_finding_worth_keeping.honest_caveat: Trimming the top two moves is itself crude and UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk; a future earnings gap is a real cost the option buyer bears. Neither figure is 'the' answer. Rule adopted: log both, and pick by whether the contract expires BEFORE the next print (use ex-gap) or SPANS it (use raw).
process_finding_worth_keeping.actions: iv_history.json now carries rv_30d_ex_top2, iv_rv_ratio_ex_top2 and largest_1d_move_in_window_pct on every row. CLAUDE.md HARD RULE 8 gained a bullet stating the rule at file level.
process_finding_worth_keeping.meta_lesson: The 2026-08-13 LIN row caught this exact artifact on ONE name and nobody generalized it, so five later runs kept citing raw ratios. the_silence_decision.question: The 13:39Z decision package asked Ryan to choose on the QQQ 21-DTE review at +$22.50/+5.6% (+$18 net). Forty-five minutes later it is +$51/+12.6% (+$48 net). Does he get a second message?
the_silence_decision.reasoning: The monitoring mandate's test is whether a trigger FIRES/UN-FIRES or the RECOMMENDATION changes -- not whether the number improved. The 13:39Z run wrote an explicit re-notify contract (ratchet 6.08, pop 7.29, setup break QQQ close >730, -50% at 2.03, backstop 1.42) and NONE fired at 4.56. I re-derived the recommendation from scratch rather than deferring to the prior run: a 21-DTE, -0.20-delta index put burning 5.4% of its mark PER DAY is a poor vehicle for a bearish view even when the view is RIGHT, which is the entire reason the 21-DTE rule exists. The tape improving fixes the VIEW; it does not fix the VEHICLE. So 'bank it' stands.
the_silence_decision.the_asymmetry_that_settles_it: A better price can only make 'bank it' MORE right, never wrong. There is no branch on which the improved number flips his decision, so a second message buys him nothing and spends the attention the silence rule exists to protect. If he replies 'close it', he simply gets a better fill than quoted.
the_silence_decision.self_check: I tested this against the opposite reading and I want it on the record, because the pull was real. There IS a genuinely new FACT here beyond price -- the brief's confirming level re-asserted -- and that fact cuts toward the HOLD alternative, which is the one branch where new information could matter. I still judged it insufficient: theta at 21 DTE dominates a delta of -0.20, and the honest risk was that I was assembling a reason to make a quiet run feel eventful. Naming that pull is the safeguard; a run that notifies every time its book ticks favourably is how 26 messages a day get ignored and the mandate dies.

A dead-man that tests LIVENESS cannot detect DEGRADATION. Binding corollary until fixed: the DTE-7 floor exists BECAUSE a 15-minute cadence cannot manage expiry-day gamma; at 60 minutes that blind spot is 4x wider, so short-DTE contracts warrant MORE caution and no run should describe the cadence as 15-minute -- it is hourly.
entries.diagnosis_handed_to_ryan: Only he can fix it; the trigger config lives on his cron-job.org account. lessons_for_the_relay: THE REPORT'S RSI2 BOARD NEEDS A 'WHY IS IT DOWN' CHECK BEFORE THE CHAIN WORK, NOT AFTER. INTC's print was manufactured by a $20B secondary. Cheapest fix available to a run today: on any RSI2 name that is down multiple sessions in a row, do the news check FIRST. It cost one web search here and killed the candidate before any thesis work.

Pick ONE convention, state it, and stick to it; the discontinuity is now on the record rather than silently corrupting a future percentile.

THE_CORRECTION_THAT_MATTERS.the_class_of_bug: This is the THIRD documented instance of the same error and CLAUDE.md already names the first two: concluding a name is untradeable from the WRONG QUOTE. the_respec.what_changed: Condition 1 relaxes from 'last >= 489.30' to 'last >= 489.00'. Condition 2 tightens from ONE completed 5-minute bar closing >= 489.30 to TWO CONSECUTIVE completed bars closing >= 489.30. Condition 3 (QQQ >= 703.00) unchanged.
the_respec.the_defect_it_fixes: The three-condition trigger requires an INSTANTANEOUS tick to sit above a precise level at the arbitrary moment a scheduled run happens to quote. At the desk's actual cadence -- 15 to 60 minutes between runs -- that is substantially a coincidence test, not a confirmation test. Two attempts have now failed partly on that coincidence: the first on a wick that did not survive (a real fail), the second on a 12.5-cent tick gap while the level had ALREADY been taken on a closing basis (a fail the plan should not want). Requiring two consecutive closes above measures the thing the plan actually cares about -- that the base top is HELD -- instead of measuring the desk's luck with the clock.
the_respec.why_this_is_not_loosening_and_the_test_t: The proof is that the new spec does NOT fire right now. The 15:20Z bar closed 487.68, so there is no pair of consecutive closes >= 489.30 and the setup stays unfired at this instant -- a re-spec written to authorize the trade the run wanted would have fired. It trades a 30-cent tick tolerance for a full extra five minutes of confirmation, which on a base-top breakout is the more expensive requirement of the two.
the_respec.FINAL_SPEC_NO_MORE_TINKERING: This is the second re-spec in three runs and that is the limit. The next change to this setup is either FIRE or VOID -- no further re-specification, no matter how narrowly it misses. A trigger edited every run is not a plan, it is a running commentary, and the drift check would rightly flag three re-specs as the preference becoming doctrine.

The correct response to a trigger that is hard to satisfy for a BAD reason (clock luck) is to fix the specification openly and prove the fix does not fire today, which is what this run did.

THE_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MOST_THIS_RUN.the_arithmetic: v4 TACTICAL specifies delta 0.40-0.60, chains <=3% of mid, and size $300-600, and says 'in practice this means SPY, QQQ, NVDA and a handful of mega-caps'. Measured today at the nearest DTE-7-compliant board: a 0.43-0.49 delta put costs $535.50 on SPY, $788.00-911.50 on QQQ, and $740.00 on NVDA. Only SPY clears $600. So the tactical track is, at ~$4.1k of equity, a SPY-ONLY track -- which quietly removes the desk's ability to scalp the index it actually forms theses about. Today the desk had a live, four-times-rejected, volume-confirmed failed-bounce trigger on QQQ, $2,773.56 of deployable cash, all five slots free and a loss cap in credit, and could not act on any of it.
THE_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MOST_THIS_RUN.the_mechanism_and_the_mistake_I_MADE_GET: Premium scales with spot x IV x sqrt(time), so affordability splits on the IV term, not the share price -- CLAUDE.md already documents this. I nonetheless PREDICTED from spot before measuring, and got it backwards: I estimated SPY at ~$690 (dearest, highest spot $764) and NVDA at ~$595 (cheapest, lowest spot $210). Measured, it is exactly inverted -- SPY is the CHEAPEST at $535.50 because its IV is 0.1257, while NVDA at a third the share price costs $740 because its IV is 0.5091, four times SPY's. This is the FOURTH occurrence of the same failure shape this file records (spot price 08-14, ATM strike 08-17, wrong expiry board 08-24 morning, and now a modelled estimate instead of a quote). The estimate cost nothing only because I measured before acting. NEVER let a computed guess stand in for a quote when the number decides a trade.
THE_FINDING_THAT_MATTERS_MOST_THIS_RUN.recommendation_for_ryan_NOT_A_DECISION_T: Flagged for Ryan's judgment; HARD RULE 9 -- no approval is claimed, quoted or implied, and this run changed nothing. The $300-600 band sits inside THE FOUR LAWS ('no thesis, no reasoning, no exception ever overrides these'), so no run may relax it and none should try. Three coherent resolutions, his call: (a) widen the tactical band to roughly $300-950 so a 0.40-0.60 delta QQQ contract becomes reachable, keeping every other tactical gate intact; (b) accept a SPY-only tactical track and route all QQQ theses to CORE -- clean, but CORE's 21-45 DTE window makes it a poor fit for hour-scale trades; or (c) permit a lower-delta QQQ strike for tactical, which is the worst of the three because it discards the delta rationale the track exists for. Recommendation: (a). It is the smallest change that restores the track's stated purpose, and it leaves the ceiling far below the $1,500 per-position maximum.

Same shape as this file's recurring bug: a check that passes for the wrong reason.

the_one_substantive_finding.the_fork: `idea` said 713.05 (the 8/20 value). `if_taken...invalidation_on_the_UNDERLYING` also said 713.05. `void_clause` and `trigger_that_would_make_it_live` said 713.4416 (the 8/21 value). Only the appended `_LEVEL_REFRESH_2026-08-25T13:05Z` carried the live 713.2256. Spread: 0.39 points across fields that are supposed to name the SAME level.
the_one_substantive_finding.why_it_mattered_operationally: This is not cosmetic. That one level does TRIPLE duty in this watch: it is the void clause (a session close above it kills the whole bearish premise), the upper bound of the failed-retest zone in trigger leg (a), and the written invalidation in the pre-committed exit plan. A post-open run reading `trigger` first would have set the retest zone to 713.44 and could have called a rejection off a tag that never reached the real level; a run reading the exit plan first would have written 713.05 as its invalidation and been ~0.18 too LOW in the other direction.
the_one_substantive_finding.root_cause: The 13:05Z run's MEASUREMENT was correct and its lesson was correct -- it caught that the inherited '+0.4/day' drift instruction was wrong in both magnitude and sign once the MA rolled over. Its DELIVERY was the defect: it appended the correction as a new sibling field instead of applying it to the four fields that carry the level. A correction placed alongside an error does not fix the error, it FORKS it.
the_one_substantive_finding.fix_applied: Verified 713.2256 INDEPENDENTLY this run rather than inheriting it (get_equity_technical_indicators sma/50/day: 8/18 712.9844 -> 8/19 712.9846 -> 8/20 713.0466 -> 8/21 713.4416 -> 8/24 713.2256; the 13:05Z series reproduces exactly). the_one_substantive_finding.the_transferable_lesson: This is CLAUDE.md's standing principle -- fix the root, don't just flag it -- applied to the ledger itself, and it is the SAME SHAPE as the lot-count invariant already written into HARD RULE 8: when one measurement changes, every derived field carrying it goes stale AT ONCE, and repairing them one incident at a time leaves the record internally inconsistent in exactly the way that is invisible to a reader checking only the field their own task touches. the_one_substantive_finding.honest_scope: This changed no trade, no position and no decision -- the watch is still unfired and the market is still closed. It removes a real trap from the path of the first post-open run, nothing more.

IV_METHOD_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.why_it_mattered_TODAY_and_not_merely_as_: QQQ's headline ratio of 0.899 reads 'index vol is on sale' and would have supplied a vol argument for buying the 50-day break. IV_METHOD_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.honest_limit: Trimming the top two moves is itself a crude estimator that UNDERSTATES fat-tail risk. Neither number is 'the' answer: for a contract expiring BEFORE the next print the ex-gap ratio is the more honest gauge; for one SPANNING a print the raw ratio is, because the buyer genuinely bears that gap. With 11 rows per core name, still under the 20-reading threshold, so IV/RV only -- no percentile is computed or cited.

the_finding_this_run_adds.what: The desk's tactical confirmation clause -- 'volume at or above the session average' -- is calibrated against a baseline the intraday volume curve makes structurally unreachable after the first hour. Measured on today's own 5-minute QQQ series (30 bars, 13:30Z-15:55Z).
the_finding_this_run_adds.the_measurement: First-hour mean 254,448/bar. Post-first-hour mean 118,481/bar -- a 53% decay. Session mean 172,868; ex-open mean 161,097. So a midday bar must trade ~1.5x the prevailing local rate merely to reach the 'average' the clause names, and ~2.1x to reach the first hour's. The clause is therefore acting as a de-facto TIME-OF-DAY filter, not a participation filter: after roughly 10:30 ET it can almost never fire, whatever the tape does.
the_finding_this_run_adds.and_here_is_the_honest_half: Correcting the baseline would have changed NO decision today, which is why this is filed as a calibration note rather than a missed trade. Against a properly local baseline (the six bars 14:55Z-15:20Z, mean 123,868): the BREAKOUT bar traded 96,113 = 77.6% of local rate, so it still fails a corrected threshold and the veto stands on both measures. The one bar that DID clear a corrected threshold -- the 15:30Z extension bar at 173,453 = 140% of local rate (and only 100.3% of the session average) -- produced an immediate and complete retracement within three bars. So on today's evidence the corrected filter would have confirmed exactly one break, and that break failed.
the_finding_this_run_adds.the_recommendation_and_its_caveat: Confirmation volume should be measured against the TRAILING 30-60 MINUTES of the same session, not the session average, because the session average embeds the opening auction and the first-hour surge. But a locally-calibrated threshold is easier to clear, so it must be paired with the price clause staying strict -- a COMPLETED close beyond the level AND holding beyond it on the following bar -- or the desk simply starts trading midday noise at a lower bar. This is a proposal for how to measure, not a loosening of what qualifies.
the_finding_this_run_adds.why_it_is_worth_writing_down: Four level-fires have been vetoed on this clause in one session. A filter that rejects everything is indistinguishable from a filter that is broken, and the only way to tell them apart is to measure the baseline rather than the outcome. Written back to CLAUDE.md so the next instance inherits the corrected method instead of re-deriving it from a fifth veto.

THE_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.the_false_constraint_this_run_nearly_wro: Having seen TLT 84C at $59.50 and XLP/XLF/XLU/XLE in the $43-86 spot range, the natural inference was that the low-priced liquid ETFs cannot produce a $300-1,000 TACTICAL or $500-1,000 CORE position and are therefore structurally excluded -- a tidy mirror of the documented 'AMD is priced out' finding, and it was about to be written into the ledger as one.
THE_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.why_it_is_wrong: Spread as a percentage of mid is a PER-CONTRACT property and is completely unaffected by quantity. Ten TLT 84C cost $595.00 -- dead centre of the CORE band -- at 1.68% of mid, with 51,155 OI and a 546 x 784 book that absorbs that size without difficulty. THE_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.what_it_opens: The entire liquid low-priced ETF universe -- TLT, XLP, XLF, XLU, XLE, and their peers -- is available to both tracks and has never been hunted. That matters most on precisely the days the desk keeps getting stuck: when index and mega-cap boards are blocked by a single-name earnings print, these instruments are uncorrelated with it AND quote tighter than anything the equity report screen produces.
THE_FINDING_WORTH_INHERITING.the_transferable_lesson_which_is_this_fi: This is the fourth documented instance of the same bug and the first one caught BEFORE it was written down rather than after. Spot price (2026-08-14), ATM strike (2026-08-17), wrong expiry board (2026-08-24 morning), and now quantity-of-one. Every instance is the same error -- declaring a name untradeable from a quote that was never the test -- and the fix is always the same: QUOTE IT. The estimate cost nothing here only because it was measured before being acted on.

THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.why_this_is_worse_than_either_defect_alo: The two stale denominators point OPPOSITE ways and mask each other. A stale-low box makes the upside clause permanently already-satisfied; a session-average volume baseline makes confirmation permanently unreachable. Netted, the trigger looks disciplined because it never fires -- while sitting one volume spike away from firing a LONG into a pre-catalyst drift on a box the desk no longer believed in. Neither defect shows up in the outcome, because the outcome is 'no trade', which is also what correct behaviour looks like.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.the_rule_written_back_to_CLAUDE_md_scope: Any trigger written with numbers in it must state the WINDOW those numbers came from, and every run must RE-DERIVE them off the last closed bars before testing it. Price and volume clauses must be measured over the SAME window -- a 15:01Z box tested against 17:00Z volume is not one trigger, it is two unrelated assertions. A run that inherits a numbered clause it did not re-derive has not tested the trigger; it has quoted it. Recorded in holdings.json durable_findings for promotion after the bell.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.honest_scope: Correcting the box changed NO decision today -- see below. THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.headline: A DESK THAT GRADES ITS ENTRIES AND NEVER AUDITS ITS DECLINES LEARNS ONLY HALF ITS PROCESS -- SO THIS RUN AUDITED ONE, AND FOUND THE DECLINE RIGHT AND THE LEVEL WRONG.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.part_1_the_decline_held_up: The 17:52Z run declined a QQQ tactical put on the 20-day loss at grade B, on four stated grounds. Measured 70 minutes later: QQQ 709.47 -> 709.33 = -0.14 points, -0.0197%. A ~0.45-delta put entered on that trigger would have earned roughly $6 of delta against ~$30-40/day of theta on an 11-DTE contract -- a net loser. Ground by ground: magnitude stayed noise-scale (confirmed); volume was drift not distribution (confirmed and WORSENED, below); SPY structure intact (confirmed -- SPY 764.93 has held a 763.05-766.78 band all session and sits mid-range); the time stop still bars the resolving event (unchanged). The decline was correct.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.part_2_volume_is_LEAVING: Re-derived off the last closed bars per the 16:05Z calibration rule rather than the session average. Trailing-30min mean 52,956/bar against a trailing-60min mean of 62,471/bar -- the recent window is only 84.8% of the wider one. The final bar (17:55Z) traded 37,599 = 71.0% of the trailing-30 mean, the quietest bar of the session. A structural break that goes nowhere across twelve consecutive bars on DECAYING participation is not a break, it is a shelf. This is the tape emptying out ahead of a print, which is the exact opposite of what a trend-initiation trade requires.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.part_3_the_level_was_wrong: SESSION LOW IS 708.88, NOT 708.77. Re-derived from the full regular-hours 30-minute series: the 15:00Z bar low is 708.880000, and a 30-minute bar's low is by construction the minimum of its constituent 5-minute lows, so this is exact for RTH. 708.77 appears in the 17:05Z box ('708.77-710.55') and in the 17:33Z run ('QQQ 709.40 sits 0.63 ABOVE the session low 708.77'). The 0.11 error is small; that it survived three runs is not. It is the ONE structural level the entire downside trigger references, and this file's own 17:22Z rule already says to re-derive the numbers a trigger is tested against instead of quoting them. Same class as every carried-constant failure in CLAUDE.md: nothing errored, and the wrong level looked exactly like the right one.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.part_4_structure_restated_correctly: QQQ 709.33 is boxed mid-band between two STRUCTURAL levels: the 20-day SMA 710.3985 sits 1.068 above and has FLIPPED FROM SUPPORT TO RESISTANCE (lost 17:00Z, unreclaimed for twelve bars, the lone retest at 17:15Z peaking 710.2999 and failing 0.0986 short); the corrected session low 708.88 sits 0.45 below. Band 1.52 points wide. Both are structural, not desk-drawn -- the distinction the 17:22Z finding was written to enforce.
THE_FINDING_THIS_RUN_ADDS.transferable_lesson: Audit a decline the same way you would audit a fill, and do it on a day the audit CONFIRMS the decision -- that is when the check is credible. The audit is also what surfaced the bad level: re-deriving the numbers to test whether the pass was right is the same work as re-deriving them to test whether the trigger fires, so the cost was zero and it caught an error three runs had passed over.

The 18:01Z run re-derived from the 30-MINUTE series and reasoned, correctly in principle, that 'a 30-minute bar's low is by construction the minimum of its constituent 5-minute lows'. the_finding.detector: Derive intraday structural levels from the 5-minute series only. the_compaction.promoted_to_CLAUDE_md: (1) The data feed itself can be wrong -- reconcile aggregated bars against the 1-MINUTE series before any level or volume clause decides a trade; the mechanism is that an aggregated bar is occasionally its LAST constituent minute, which corrupts PRICE as well as volume, and a hole biases confirmation toward FALSE POSITIVES. (2) Compute BOTH the 20- and 50-day SMA before drawing any intraday box -- a box that keeps producing failed breaks is usually a moving average nobody measured -- plus the roll-off corollary that a correctly re-derived level can itself be moving fast. (5) min_ticks is a free liquidity pre-screen, valid in ONE direction only. (6) The equity report's RSI2 names are now measured twice at roughly zero options-tradeability. entries.near_miss_the_diff_stat_rule_caught: Worth one line because it is the detector working as designed. Writing the union merge, this run SORTED entries[] by run_utc 'to keep them ordered' -- and `git diff --numstat` came back 96 insertions / 65 DELETIONS for what should have been a pure append. The sort had relocated the 2026-08-25T18:18:00Z entry, which was deliberately appended AFTER its 18:20Z sibling and says so in its own _ordering_note ('read them by run_utc, not by position'). Reverted to append-only: 31 insertions, 0 deletions. THE LESSON IS THE ONE ALREADY IN CLAUDE.md AND IT GENERALISES PAST SERIALIZATION: the diff stat catches any change larger than the one you meant to make, not just an indent or ensure_ascii mismatch. Ordering is content in an append-only log. Trust the stat line, not the intention.

durable_finding_1_minute_feed_is_NOT_an_.claim_being_corrected: CLAUDE.md's feed rule (set 2026-08-25T19:00Z) fixes the defect where an aggregated 5- or 30-minute bar is silently its last constituent minute, and prescribes reconciling against the 1-minute series because 'the 1-minute series is the arbiter and every coarser interval is a convenience.' MEASURED TODAY: the 1-minute series has the SAME defect, so it is the best available series, not an arbiter.
durable_finding_1_minute_feed_is_NOT_an_.measurement: QQQ 2026-08-26T14:11Z, one bar, three fetches. Fetch at ~14:26Z returned volume 10,006 with OHLC open 710.630 / high 710.760 / low 710.521 / close 710.521. Fetches at ~14:29Z and ~14:31Z both returned volume 453 with OHLC open 710.545 / high 710.570 / low 710.545 / close 710.560. That is a -95.5% volume revision, and a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT OHLC, on a bar that had been closed for fifteen minutes. Both readings cannot be right, and the later one -- a 453-share, 0.025-point-range bar wedged between neighbours of 20,981 and 29,138 -- has the exact single-tick signature the original rule teaches you to recognise in coarser intervals. Smaller same-window revisions were seen simultaneously on 13:46 (33,903 -> 34,243), 13:57 (24,976 -> 25,116), 14:13 (23,098 -> 23,723), 14:22 (33,878 -> 32,437) and 14:23 (10,330 -> 28,424).
durable_finding_1_minute_feed_is_NOT_an_.why_it_matters_and_the_honest_size_of_it: It moves the number a volume clause is decided on. The same candidate bucket scored 104.4% of its trailing-30 mean on the fetch-1 numbers and 105.7% on the fetch-2/3 numbers -- both above the line here, so it changed NO decision today, which is precisely why it is safe to trust as a measurement. On a borderline reading it flips the answer, and the direction is not predictable: revision went both up and down within one window.
durable_finding_1_minute_feed_is_NOT_an_.the_detector: Two cheap defences, either sufficient. (a) Fetch the window TWICE a few minutes apart and compare before letting a volume clause decide; disagreement means provisional, not quiet. (b) End the trailing baseline window ~10 minutes back from now rather than at the last printed bar, so the clause is computed only on settled bars. And the recognition rule generalises down one level: a 1-MINUTE bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours is provisional, not a quiet minute -- the same test the existing rule applies to 5-minute buckets.
durable_finding_1_minute_feed_is_NOT_an_.transferable_lesson: The 2026-08-25 rule correctly refused to trust an interval just because it was fine-grained, then made the finest available interval the arbiter anyway. There is no arbiter in a live feed -- only settled data and a reconciliation. Trust the agreement between two reads, not the granularity of one.

durable_findings.the_first_large_UPWARD_1_minute_revision:
MEASURED 2026-08-26T15:32Z, and it completes today's 14:31Z finding from the opposite direction. That earlier run proved 1-minute bars are revised after they close (a -95.5% volume revision with a changed OHLC) and noted revisions 'ran both up and down' without having measured a large up-side case. Here it is: QQQ's 15:29Z bar, read twice ONE MINUTE APART, went from volume 1,756 / open 710.450 / high 710.450 / close 710.400 to volume 12,835 / open 710.590 / high 710.660 / close 710.470 -- a +630.9% volume revision with a different OHLC. It carries the exact signature the rule teaches: a bar whose volume is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours (7,968 and 22,840) is PROVISIONAL, not a quiet minute. Three other bars in the same window revised materially (15:14 -13.9%, 15:18 +10.7%, 15:26 -4.7%), so this is a live property of the feed, not a one-off.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE NEW LESSON, AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE EXISTING FIX. The 'end the trailing baseline ~10 minutes back' rule protects the DENOMINATOR and nothing else. A provisional bar in the last minutes of the CANDIDATE window sits inside the numerator and outside a baseline that already ended ten minutes ago, so its revision is ONE-SIDED by construction. Measured exactly here: the revision moved the candidate 5-minute bar +28.6% (37,572 -> 48,331) while moving the baseline -0.11% (94,849 -> 94,749), lifting the confirmation reading from 39.7% to 51.0% of baseline. That is the FALSE-POSITIVE direction -- the same dangerous direction as the dropped-bucket defect, arriving through the opposite mechanism.

THE FIX, symmetric with the one already in the playbook: the final bar of a candidate window is the single bar most likely to be provisional AND the one whose revision cannot be offset. So either end the CANDIDATE window ~10 minutes back as well, or double-read its constituent minutes before letting it confirm. This run did the latter -- two fetches a minute apart, merged, disagreements resolved to the later read.

HONEST SCOPE, and it is what makes the audit credible: this changed NO decision today. The price clause failed outright, and 51% of baseline still fails the volume clause decisively. A filter's inputs can only be audited honestly on a day the correction does not flip the answer -- and the uncorrected 39.7% would have supported a stronger 'volume has collapsed' claim than the data actually carries, which is the small dishonesty this catch prevents.
durable_findings.pre_event_volume_vacuum_is_a_measurable_: Participation halving in thirty minutes on a flat index (94,749 -> 48,331 per 5-minute bar, monotonic over four bars) is a measurement, and it makes a specific forward prediction rather than a vibe: any level break arriving in this state cannot clear a volume-confirmation clause calibrated on a live baseline, so the tactical track is effectively closed until participation returns. State that as the reason for standing down, rather than reporting 'no trigger' as though the tape were merely quiet -- the two look identical from the outside and only one of them tells the next instance what to watch for.
durable_findings.a_trigger_keyed_to_the_prior_day_close_s: Worth recording before a future run treats today's near-misses as meaningful. QQQ's completed 5-minute closes crossed the 710.72 prior-day close FOUR times before 14:10Z (below at 13:30/13:35, above 13:40, below 13:45, above 13:50-14:05, below since), and price has spent the last fourteen bars inside 709.09-710.71, i.e. hugging just under it. A 'close above the prior close' clause on such a day fires on the morning drift and then goes silent while price oscillates a penny beneath it -- it is measuring the tape's noise amplitude, not a decision. The prior close IS a structural level, which is why it was correctly chosen over a desk-drawn box; the point is narrower and still real: STRUCTURAL IS NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. A structural level that today's price has already closed on both sides of several times has no remaining information in it, and the 0.010 near-miss at 15:05Z should be read as chop touching a magnet, not as a setup one tick from triggering.

The 2026-08-25 calibration rule rightly replaced a session-average denominator with a trailing-local one because the opening hour made midday fires impossible; nobody checked the other end. A trailing-local mean tracks a draining tape downward, so in a pre-event vacuum the clause stops asking 'did participation arrive' and starts asking 'is this bar busier than the vacuum', which any drift toward normal satisfies. durable_findings.THE REAL LEGGING HAZARD IS CORRELATION,: Both legs are the same underlying and expiry, five strikes apart, so they are ~95% correlated. When the tape moves against the long leg after it fills, the credit available on leg two shrinks AT THE SAME TIME. Measured on 735P 1-minute bars while the sibling chased: 16:55 close 2.88, 16:56 close 2.84, 16:57 close 2.81, 17:00 close 2.79 -- an 11-cent slide in six minutes, with every one of its limits (2.90/2.89/2.86) sitting at or ABOVE the entire subsequent bar's range. This is not a chase that was too slow. It is a chase that cannot win, because the thing being chased moves for the same reason the long leg is losing. Legging risk is directional and self-reinforcing, not symmetric.
durable_findings.THE ORPHAN'S RISK IS THE LONG LEG'S NOTI: The intended vertical's ENTIRE max loss was $65 (net debit 3.51 - 2.86). The failed legging burned $13 -- 20% of the whole trade's risk budget -- in under 7 minutes, without ever holding the position. The orphan carried delta -0.1906 on a $764.81 underlying = ~$146 of P/L per 1% SPY move, so a 0.5% SPY move inside that window would have cost ~$73: MORE than the vertical's entire max loss, on a position nobody graded. A cheap, tight, defined-risk vertical becomes an UNDEFINED-risk trade the moment it is legged.
durable_findings.What atomicity is actually buying: Everything above. Handing a spec to Ryan to place in the app is not a workaround for a missing API feature -- it is how the desk buys atomic execution, which is the entire product a multi-leg order sells. Net-debit slippage for completeness: target 0.65, achievable 0.68 at 16:57 and 0.72 at 17:00, so even a successful late fill widens max loss $65 -> $72 (+10.8%) on a market quoting ONE CENT wide. Small in dollars, large in percent-of-risk, and percent-of-risk is the only unit that matters on a defined-risk trade.
durable_findings.Credit where it is due, and say this to: The sibling got the ordering right (long leg first, so a naked short was never possible), used correct position_effect on every order, recognised its own orphan within ~5 minutes, and unwound it by walking the limit 3.41 -> 3.40 -> 3.38 to fill at the midpoint -- exactly the exit-pricing discipline Ryan set on 2026-07-21. A governance breach that self-corrects at a $13 cost is a very different thing from a runaway, and reporting only the breach would misrepresent it.

Semis are unambiguously leading: SMH +2.03%, AVGO +2.98%, TSM +1.30%, NVDA +7.25%. On today's settled tape the breadth limb CONFIRMS the semi trade; it does not diverge from it.
CORRECTION_to_the_13_37Z_verdict.the_transferable_defect: THE RE-QUOTE RULE WAS APPLIED TO THE POSITION MARK BUT NOT TO THE CROSS-SECTIONAL BREADTH READ THAT DECIDED A TRADE GATE. The 13:37Z run explicitly and correctly re-took its own quotes past the 13:30Z auction and discarded the 13:31:10Z batch as auction prints -- then built its breadth verdict on complex readings taken in that same first four minutes. CLAUDE.md's re-quote rule was written from a POSITION-MARK incident (the 2026-08-21 QQQ 680P, where the sign of the P/L was wrong), and it has been faithfully applied to marks ever since. Nobody extended it to the OTHER thing a four-minute-old tape is used for: a breadth or leadership judgment. A cross-sectional read at minute four is at least as unsettled as a mark at minute four -- arguably more, because it aggregates several unsettled opens. RULE: the ~5-minutes-past-13:30Z re-quote discipline governs ANY number that gates a decision, not only a position mark. If a run cites percentage day-changes across a complex to confirm or refute a setup, those figures must be settled ones. This is the same shape as every other entry in this file's 'a check that passes for the wrong reason' family: the right rule, applied to one artifact and not the adjacent one.
CORRECTION_to_the_13_37Z_verdict.does_the_correction_change_the_answer: NO, and saying so plainly is the point -- an audit of a prior run's inputs is only credible when performed where it does not conveniently flip the verdict. NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.subject: A THIRD DISTINCT DEFECT IN THE TACTICAL VOLUME-CONFIRMATION DENOMINATOR, and unlike the first two it is not a calibration error -- it is that NO baseline is computable at all in the first ~20 minutes of a session.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.the_measurement: QQQ 1-minute volumes, 2026-08-27 session, candidate bar 13:45 = 83,723. Trailing baseline EXCLUDING the six opening bars (13:36-13:44, 9 bars): mean 62,335 -> the candidate reads 134.3% and CONFIRMS. Trailing baseline INCLUDING every bar from the 13:30 open (15 bars, opening bar 257,443): mean 86,293 -> the identical candidate reads 97.0% and FAILS. The confirmation verdict flips across the line on a single judgment call about which bars belong in the window -- and NOTHING about the tape changed between the two computations.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.why_this_is_new: The 2026-08-25T16:05Z finding showed the SESSION-AVERAGE denominator is too STRICT because the opening hour inflates it. The 2026-08-26T15:52Z finding showed the TRAILING-LOCAL denominator inverts and becomes too LOOSE in a decaying tape. Both are about a baseline that EXISTS being mis-specified. This is the case where the required window -- the trailing 30 to 60 minutes -- simply has not elapsed, so every available substitute is a construct chosen by the run that needs it. A run wanting to trade can pick the 9-bar window and pass; a run wanting to decline can pick the full window and fail. That is not a filter, it is a rationalisation surface.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.the_rule: NO TACTICAL VOLUME-CONFIRMATION CLAUSE IS COMPUTABLE UNTIL AT LEAST ~30 MINUTES OF POST-OPENING-BAR DATA EXIST -- in practice not before roughly 10:00-10:05 ET. Before that, the correct output is 'the clause cannot be evaluated', NOT a substitute baseline. Do not construct one. If a level breaks in the first half hour and the setup is otherwise compelling, say plainly that confirmation is unavailable and let the trade go; the opening range is the most whipsaw-prone window of the day and the arc above shows the desk loses on clean-looking breaks even with a valid denominator.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.the_self_check_that_caught_it: This run built the 9-bar excluding-the-open baseline FIRST, got 134.3%, and noticed it was about to report a PASS off a window it had chosen. FOUR LAWS: 'if you ever find yourself constructing an argument for why one of these shouldn't apply right now, that is the signal to stop.' The generalisation is that constructing a DENOMINATOR to satisfy a clause is the same act as constructing an argument to evade a law. Computing the alternative window took one line and inverted the answer.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_does_not_exi.also_the_bars_are_provisional: Independently disqualifying: the 13:44 and 13:45 bars were minutes old at read time, and the 2026-08-26T14:31Z measurement showed a closed 1-minute bar revising -95.5% in volume with a wholly different OHLC fifteen minutes after it closed. The two-read detector was not run because the magnitude decline settled the trade first -- recorded so the next run does not mistake this for a validated reading.

entries.transferable_lesson: WHEN A SINGLE MEGA-CAP'S DAY-CHANGE FLIPS HARD, MEASURE THE BROAD INDEX OVER THE SAME MINUTES BEFORE CALLING IT BREADTH. A constituent's move and the market's move are different claims, and the constituent is the one that moves first and looks most like news -- so the tempting inference (a big name reversing means participation is broadening) is available precisely when it is least likely to be true. The detector costs one extra symbol and one aligned window: pull SPY over the identical bars. Here MSFT +1.55% against SPY +0.066% turned an apparent refutation of the morning's narrow-breadth finding into a confirmation of it. This is the same family as the file's existing regime-label staleness rule, arriving from the opposite direction: that one warns a stale label can survive a reversal, this one warns a live label can be discarded on a single constituent's move.

NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.subject: ANOMALY-EXCLUSION FROM THE VOLUME BASELINE BIASES CONFIRMATION IN THE SAME FALSE-POSITIVE DIRECTION AS BASELINE COLLAPSE -- AND UNLIKE THE FIRST TWO DEFECTS, THIS ONE IS PUT THERE BY THE DESK, EVERY RUN, WITHOUT BEING NOTED.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.the_two_known_defects: The denominator has been corrected twice. (1) 2026-08-25T16:05Z: a SESSION-AVERAGE baseline is too STRICT, because the opening hour inflates it -- fixed by using a trailing 30-60 minute local mean. (2) 2026-08-26T15:52Z: a trailing-LOCAL baseline INVERTS in a decaying tape, getting easier exactly where it should get harder -- fixed by requiring the candidate bar to clear BOTH the trailing local mean AND the session's established bucket rate.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.the_third_defect: Both fixes are about WHICH WINDOW. Neither addresses what the desk does INSIDE the window. Every run today has computed its baseline 'anomaly-excluded' -- the 13:48Z run excluded the opening bars, the 14:00Z and 14:20Z runs excluded the 13:59 spike -- and none stated the effect on the bar-to-clear. Measured this run on the 13:46-14:15 settled window: INCLUDING the 13:59 bar the trailing-30 mean is 58,070/bar; EXCLUDING it, 47,473/bar. Trimming one bar of thirty lowered the bar to clear by 18.3%.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.why_it_is_not_the_same_as_the_data_hole_: The 2026-08-25T19:00Z reconciliation rule tells a run to substitute the 1-minute sum for a DEFECTIVE bucket -- a dropped bar, a bar whose volume equals one constituent minute. That is repairing corrupt data and it is correct. The 13:59 bar is the opposite: 365,380 shares, re-fetched BYTE-IDENTICAL at three separate times now (14:00Z, ~14:04Z, and this run at 14:26Z, 27 minutes later), carrying a real 20-day-tag reversal. It is the single most REAL bar of the session. Excluding it is not data repair -- it is trimming the fat tail of the very distribution the filter exists to measure.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.why_the_direction_matters: A participation filter asks 'is this bar busier than normal'. Removing the busiest bars from 'normal' makes every later bar look busier by comparison. That is the SAME directional bias as the 2026-08-26 baseline-collapse defect -- toward FALSE POSITIVES, toward confirming breaks that should not confirm -- arriving through a different mechanism, and it stacks with it rather than offsetting it. A decaying tape lowers the denominator; trimming its peaks lowers it again.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.why_it_survived: The habit is imported from the IV method, where trimming the top two moves (rv_30d_ex_top2) is CORRECT -- there, one earnings gap genuinely dominates a 30-sample stdev and the trimmed number is the more honest one. The two look identical and are not: realized vol is trying to estimate a typical day and an event gap is a contaminant, whereas a participation baseline is trying to estimate what real interest looks like and a high-volume bar IS the thing being estimated. This file already warns that a rule written to stop trusting one convenient number can replace it with a different convenient number.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.the_rule: Report BOTH the trimmed and untrimmed baseline, always, and say which bars were removed and why. Trim ONLY bars the reconciliation shows are DEFECTIVE (dropped buckets, single-tick signatures, provisional revisions). A genuine high-volume bar STAYS IN -- and where a run judges an exclusion legitimate, the candidate must clear the UNTRIMMED denominator too, because a filter that gets to choose its own comparison set is not a filter.
NEW_FINDING_the_denominator_defect_the_d.honest_scope_it_changed_nothing_today: This is recorded on a day it flips no decision, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. The approach into the session high ran 29,373/bar = 61.9% of the trimmed 47,473 AND 50.6% of the untrimmed 58,070. It fails on both denominators, by a wide margin, and the price limb was unmet regardless. The defect is real, latent, and would decide a borderline case in the wrong direction.

findings_written_to_master.1_neighbour_ratio_is_a_denominator_free_: Three sessions of argument about the volume DENOMINATOR (session-average too strict, trailing-local inverting in a decaying tape, anomaly-exclusion biasing false-positive) were all disputes about what to divide BY. This break needed no denominator: 2,698 against neighbours of 28,980 and 24,243 fails against ANY baseline a participant in that argument could have constructed. THE PREFILTER, free because the bars are already in hand: before computing any trailing mean, compare the candidate bar to the two bars either side of it; if it is below roughly half of BOTH, decline on that alone. Compute the mean only where the calibration question is load-bearing. This is worth more than another calibration fix because a test invariant to the disputed parameter cannot be argued with. SCOPE: it only ever REJECTS -- a bar that clears its neighbours still needs the full dual test unchanged.
findings_written_to_master.2_provisional_bars_can_manufacture_a_pha: New sub-case, the MIRROR of the recorded one. The 2026-08-25T19:00Z case is a defective bar HIDING a real extreme (a session low that never showed). A defective bar can equally MANUFACTURE one: an isolated tick at 719.12 becomes, in the bar record, a 'completed close above the level' -- exactly the price limb of the TACTICAL test. A run applying the price limb alone would have read a clean structural break out of an artifact. WHY THE DUAL TEST CATCHES IT, and this is the argument for keeping both limbs: the same defect that fakes the price limb also collapses the volume limb, because a one-tick bar has one tick's volume. The limbs fail TOGETHER from a single cause -- so the dual test is a self-consistency check, not merely two filters stacked for strictness.
findings_written_to_master.3_breadth_not_the_event_calendar_explain: The 2026-08-26T17:19Z capstone concluded 'do not open TACTICAL breakout scalps into an unresolved scheduled catalyst', on the mechanism that pre-event positioning flow is not directional. That mechanism predicts breaks stop failing once the event clears. THE EVENT CLEARED -- NVDA reported last night and is +7.73% today -- and the ninth attempt fired and reversed anyway, on the same signature. A pre-event vacuum cannot explain a post-event failure. PROPOSED REPLACEMENT: breadth. An index ~87% driven by two names has no broad participation to carry a level break, because the other ninety-odd constituents are not moving -- so the thin-volume breaks and the narrow leadership are ONE fact seen twice, which the desk kept reading as a measurement problem rather than as the finding. DETECTOR: before any index breakout, compute the top-1-or-2 contribution share; above ~70% treat the index's own levels as carrying no information -- trade the leader or do not trade. Explains cleanly why the arc clusters on QQQ rather than SPY (higher concentration degrades first). EPISTEMIC STATUS, stated so it is not inherited as settled: ONE observation, resting on approximate index weights. A hypothesis that OUTPERFORMS the incumbent, not a fact -- falsifiable, and if breaks keep failing on a genuinely broad day then breadth is not the mechanism either and the desk should stop theorising and simply stop trading index breakouts in this regime.

A filter with a directional bias and a tape with no follow-through produce IDENTICAL evidence when you only ever test one direction -- which is why three sessions of denominator tuning could never settle it. A DOWNSIDE break, confirmed by 3.4x on the untrimmed baseline and cleared on all four denominators, failing in exactly the same way, is the first observation that DISCRIMINATES: the filter is not directionally biased, and the non-follow-through is a property of the tape. the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.what_the_capstone_said: The 2026-08-26T17:19Z capstone attributed non-follow-through to a PRE-EVENT POSITIONING VACUUM -- participation arrives at a level to de-risk into a scheduled catalyst, then stops, because nobody expresses a view before the number. the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.the_measured_replacement_one_minute_lead: NVDA LED QQQ BY A FULL BAR, DOWN AND BACK UP. NVDA: 14:35 close 225.220 -> 14:36 224.875 -> 14:37 224.730 -> 14:38 close 223.980 on 601,715 shares (its heaviest minute of the window) -> 14:39 close 223.720, low 223.500 (the bottom). the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.controls_run_over_the_IDENTICAL_minutes: SPY on the 14:39 bar: 769.625 -> 769.360 = -0.034%, and by 14:46 it printed 769.740, i.e. FULLY RECOVERED AND HIGHER than before the break. the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.the_reading: The 14:39 'index breakdown' was not an index-level decision at all. It was NVDA giving back part of its gap, one minute earlier, dragging QQQ mechanically -- and QQQ stopped falling the instant NVDA did. The 93,770 shares are real participation, but what they are participating IN is a single-name oscillation wearing an index wrapper. This explains the whole ten-attempt arc without needing the vacuum story: the index has had no independent flow today, so every 'level break' is a derivative of NVDA's post-gap chop and mean-reverts on NVDA's next tick.
the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.THE_TRANSFERABLE_RULE: LEAD/LAG TEST, and it costs one extra symbol and one extra minute of bars. Before taking any index-level break, check whether a single dominant constituent moved FIRST. If the constituent leads the index by a bar or more at the break, THE LEVEL IS NOT WHAT BROKE -- the constituent is, and the level carries no information. Decline the index trade. If the thesis is genuinely there, trade the constituent directly, because the index version is a lagged, diluted, unhedged bet on the same thing with the level-break framing supplying false confidence on top. This is the sibling of the 14:20Z 'measure the broad index over the SAME minutes before calling it breadth' detector, run in the opposite direction: that one tests whether a constituent's move IS the market's; this one tests whether the market's move is merely a constituent's.
the_mechanism_MEASURED_and_it_is_not_the.honest_scope: This changed NO decision this run -- the fire was already declined on the price limb (desk-drawn level) before the lead/lag was computed, and the follow-through failed independently. That is the only condition under which a mechanism claim can be audited credibly. It is offered as a better-evidenced replacement for the capstone's stated mechanism, not as a new reason to have traded. The lead/lag is measured on ONE event; it should be re-tested on the next index break rather than promoted to doctrine on a single observation.

LLY cleared every gate on its own merits: signal-sourced from the committed report, thesis researched to INTACT against a specific and COMPLETED cause, earnings window verified clean against a 31-day calendar rather than assumed from a blank column, cash floor computed before sizing at 87.2% against a 45% requirement, zero correlation to the existing book, and an intraday structure that confirms rather than diverges. entries.self_critique: Two honest weaknesses in this decision, recorded so the next instance can judge it on process. (1) The bounce is on LIGHT volume: ~189k shares in the first 90 minutes against a ~2.5M daily norm, roughly 7.5% of a session in the window that usually carries 20-25%. A low-participation recovery is weaker evidence than a high-participation one, and this run did NOT let the 14:30Z volume push stand as more than it is. (2) I reached the opposite conclusion mid-analysis on the day-change figure before measuring the intraday bars, and the reversal is the ONLY reason limb (c) passes. That is the correct order of operations by luck of checking, not by design -- the transferable rule, which this file already states for regime labels and now applies to a single name: NEVER let a full-day percentage change decide a limb near a fresh event; pull the intraday series, because the day change averages the selling and the absorption into a number that describes neither.

the_finding_of_this_run.transferable: When a newly-minted discriminator is about to reject a candidate, MEASURE it rather than invoke it, and if the measurement disagrees with the decision, publish the disagreement and decline on the grounds that actually hold. A test written up only when it agrees with the decision is a rationalization with a number attached. This is the file's 'check that passes for the wrong reason' family, arriving from the other side: a check that would have FAILED for the right reason.
the_finding_of_this_run.sharpened_by_the_collision: The collision SHARPENED this finding rather than duplicating it. The sibling reached the OPPOSITE tape reading on the same discriminator using a RELATIVE comparator (SCHW diverging 1.11pp negative from XLF) where this run used an ABSOLUTE one (session low 0.895 ABOVE the gap-day low, four-bar base on declining volume). Both measurements are honest and they disagree. THE REAL FINDING IS THEREFORE STRONGER THAN THE ONE ORIGINALLY WRITTEN: the completed-vs-ongoing discriminator is COMPARATOR-DEPENDENT, so a run that does not state its comparator gets whichever answer its unstated denominator favours. That is the same denominator defect this file has already documented three times in the volume-confirmation clause, arriving now inside a thesis test.

data_integrity_finding.subject: THE BYTE-IDENTITY DETECTOR FOR A DEFECTIVE 5-MINUTE BUCKET IS SOUND WHEN IT FIRES AND UNSOUND AS A SCREEN -- one of three holes found this run defeats it.
data_integrity_finding.measured: Reconciled against the 1-minute series: QQQ 14:50 bucket reported 6,978 vs a true 87,192 (8.0%); SPY 14:40 reported 6,533 vs 55,769 (11.7%); SPY 14:50 reported 15,896 vs 124,253 (12.8%). Three holes in a 27-bar two-symbol sample, all in a -87% to -92% band, categorically separate from ordinary drift.
data_integrity_finding.the_defeating_case: SPY's 14:50 bucket is byte-identical to its 14:54 constituent minute and the prescribed detector catches it. QQQ's 14:50 bucket is NOT: vol 6,978 against that minute's 7,823, and matching open and low to four decimals but not high, close or volume. It is the last minute caught MID-SETTLEMENT -- the provisional-bar defect and the dropped-bucket defect in one bar.
data_integrity_finding.why_it_matters_beyond_volume: The bucket being one minute rather than five means it cannot show the interval's extremes: QQQ's true 14:50 range is 717.840-718.900 and it reported 718.07-718.30, hiding 0.60 of the high. That mechanism once put a wrong session low on master.
data_integrity_finding.the_rule: Keep the identity test as a fast POSITIVE indicator; never use it as the screen. Sum the constituent 1-minute bars and compare -- anything off by more than ~5% is a hole. A NEAR-miss on the identity test is evidence FOR the defect, not against it.
data_integrity_finding.honest_scope: Changed no decision. None of the three defective buckets falls in the trailing-30-minute window a confirmation clause would use now, and no trigger fired on any measure today. Logged because the defect rate (3 in 27) is materially higher than the 1-in-7 previously recorded.

THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.claim: EVERY 2026-08-27 IV ROW WAS MEASURED INSIDE THE OPENING WINDOW THIS PLAYBOOK FORBIDS PRICING DECISIONS FROM, AND FIFTEEN CORE DECLINES RESTED ON THEM.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.how_it_was_found: Not from a symptom -- from asking what the repeated CORE decline was actually measured from. iv_history.json answers directly: the 2026-08-27 rows carry _sibling_cross_validation notes timestamping them to 13:31-13:41Z, one to eleven minutes after the bell.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.the_rule_that_was_broken: CLAUDE.md says it twice: 'opening prints inflate ATM IV via wide auction markets', and 'NEVER price a decision off the opening auction print -- re-quote at least ~5 minutes after 13:30Z first'. The second was written after a 13:30:08Z position mark reported the WRONG SIGN to Ryan. It was applied to position marks and never to the IV rows, which are quote-derived numbers with identical exposure.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.measurement: Re-quoted 16:02:58Z on the SAME 2026-09-25 board. FIXED STRIKE (isolates time-of-day, strike held constant): SPY 768 0.120104 vs 0.123233 = -2.54%; QQQ 716 0.178889 vs 0.183881 = -2.72%. TRUE ATM STRIKE (the honest decision input): SPY 771 0.118017 = -4.23%; QQQ 719 0.176579 = -3.97%. The ATM move is larger because spot rose and the ATM strike travelled up the skew; the fixed-strike figure is the clean estimate of the artifact.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.effect_on_the_decision: Ex-gap ratios fall SPY 1.1988 -> 1.1480 and QQQ 1.1031 -> 1.0593 -- BOTH still above 1.0, so index premium remains rich and the CORE decline stands on corrected inputs. Raw ratios fall SPY 1.0035 -> 0.9611 and QQQ 0.8533 -> 0.8194, which is exactly why the pair must be read together: raw SPY now crosses below 1.0 and would read 'cheap' alone, while the ex-gap number governing a board that expires before the next print says otherwise.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.transferable_lesson: A HYGIENE RULE WRITTEN ABOUT ONE ARTIFACT CLASS SILENTLY FAILS TO REACH EVERY OTHER NUMBER DERIVED FROM THE SAME QUOTES. The no-opening-print rule was learned from a position mark and filed as a position-marking rule; ATM IV, structural levels and spread-derived liquidity verdicts drawn in the same minutes inherit the identical defect. When a rule names the artifact that bit you, ask what ELSE is computed from that input before considering it applied.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.second_finding: CROSS-VALIDATION IS NOT BIAS VALIDATION. The rows cite two runs agreeing to ~0.0003 vol points and it reads as reassurance. Agreement establishes REPRODUCIBILITY and says nothing about BIAS -- both reads came from the same distorted window, so they agree with each other and are both distorted. The sibling notes are preserved unedited: accurate about precision, they simply never licensed the conclusion drawn from them.
THE_FINDING_IV_ROWS_MEASURED_IN_THE_FORB.honest_scope: THE AUDIT CHANGED NO DECISION TODAY, which is the condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. On a borderline reading a 4% IV error flips a CORE entry, and the bias is systematic rather than random: opening prints push IV UP, so the artifact makes premium look RICHER than it is and its failure mode is a MISSED long-premium entry, never a bad one. That benign direction is precisely why it survived fifteen runs unnoticed.

finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.subject: THE 14:25Z ANOMALY-EXCLUSION RULE HAS A HOLE, AND THIS RUN MEASURED A BAR THAT FALLS STRAIGHT THROUGH IT. That rule says: trim ONLY bars the reconciliation shows are DEFECTIVE, because a genuine high-volume bar IS the thing the participation baseline estimates. That is right about the case it was written on and silent about this one.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.measurement: SPY 1-minute bar 2026-08-27T17:18Z: volume 117,447 = 8.8x the 30-bar median (13,292); range 0.1020 = 0.85x the median range (0.1197); |close - open| = 0.0050. Re-fetched four minutes later it returned BYTE-IDENTICAL volume and OHLC, while six ordinary bars in the same window revised by 2-10% across the same pair of reads. So it is NOT defective, NOT provisional, and by the existing rule must be KEPT.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.cost_of_keeping_it: Trailing-30 mean rises from 17,207 to 20,549 -- a 19.4% inflation of the bar every later candidate must clear, in the SUPPRESSIVE direction (genuine confirmations rejected). Had a break instead LANDED on such a bar, the identical artifact would MANUFACTURE confirmation. Both failure modes, from one defect, pointing opposite ways -- which is why counting fires cannot detect it.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.the_discriminator: PARTICIPATION MOVES VOLUME AND RANGE TOGETHER; A CROSS MOVES ONLY VOLUME. The 13:59Z bar the existing rule correctly protects had 365,380 shares AND a large range AND a real 20-day-tag reversal. This bar has 8.8x volume, BELOW-median range and a half-cent net move: shares changed hands and nothing was expressed. It is a block print, not interest.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.the_test: Denominator-free, costs nothing because the bars are already in hand. Flag any bar in the top decile of volume whose RANGE is at or below the median AND whose |close - open| is a small fraction of that range. Such a bar (a) may NEVER satisfy a confirmation clause, and (b) SHOULD be excluded from the trailing baseline -- the one legitimate exception to the do-not-trim rule. State BOTH baselines when excluding, exactly as the existing key already requires.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.it_is_the_mirror_of_the_neighbour_ratio_: The pair now covers both tails: the neighbour-ratio prefilter REJECTS a candidate far BELOW both neighbours; this rejects a bar far ABOVE both neighbours that carries no range. Neither needs a denominator, so neither can be argued with on calibration grounds -- which is the property that made the prefilter worth more than another calibration fix.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.secondary_signature_offered_weakly: The block bar did not revise across two fetches while its ordinary neighbours did -- consistent with a cross reporting once and complete, where continuous trading dribbles in. Suggestive, NOT sufficient: the 14:32Z finding already established that byte identity is not a reliable detector in the other direction, so do not promote this to a test.
finding_1_A_GENUINE_HIGH_VOLUME_BAR_CAN_.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION TODAY. No level broke after 17:10Z, so no confirmation clause was reached and the inflated denominator gated nothing. That is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly, and it is the standard the 14:25Z measurement set for itself. Latent, not active. Recorded onto the EXISTING anomaly-exclusion key rather than as a new one, per the compaction rule that a contribution which completes an existing key edits that key.

new_finding_feed_hole_is_cross_symbol.why_it_matters: The 2026-08-25 root-cause bullet established that aggregated bars are occasionally a single constituent minute rather than the aggregate, and prescribed reconciling against the 1-minute series -- then the 2026-08-26 correction showed the 1-minute series has the SAME defect and is revised after close, leaving 'fetch twice and compare' as the defence. This adds a THIRD, cheaper defence: the defect lands on the same TIMESTAMP across instruments, so a second symbol at the same timestamp corroborates or refutes a suspicious bar in the SAME call that fetched it (this tool takes up to 10 symbols at once, so the check is free).
new_finding_feed_hole_is_cross_symbol.the_qualifier_that_keeps_it_honest: XLF printed NORMALLY in the identical holed window. So the rule is ASYMMETRIC and must be read in one direction only: AGREEMENT across two or more symbols at one timestamp is strong evidence of a feed-window hole; a SINGLE CLEAN symbol is NOT evidence the window is clean for the symbol you actually care about. Reading it in the permissive direction would manufacture exactly the false-confidence failure this file has now recorded four times (spot price, ATM strike, wrong expiry board, modelled estimate vs quote).
new_finding_feed_hole_is_cross_symbol.changed_no_decision: Stated plainly, to the same standard the 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-26 baseline audits set for themselves: correcting the 18:45Z bucket changes nothing today. Only a post-close run can do it, and doing it here means tomorrow's brief inherits a number instead of a mood.

AMD -1.52% and MSFT -1.10% trade DOWN and SPY manages +0.21%', and the NVDA decline cited 'the tape is fading it' as one of three grounds. A correct verdict defended by a false observation is a process finding, because the false observation is what survives into the next call -- and this is the same shape as every 'a check that passes for the wrong reason' entry in CLAUDE.md, arriving this time on the desk's own regime label.

CONTRIBUTION_2_late_entry_detector_quote.THE_GENERAL_FORM: A breakout entry taken late does not merely have a worse price -- it has its STOP PUSHED BACKWARDS ONTO THE TRIGGER LEVEL, so the position can no longer be wrong about TIMING without being wrong about THESIS. The edge in a breakout trigger is that the level supplies a cheap invalidation; entering far above it spends exactly that edge. Compute where the -30% stop lands ON THE UNDERLYING before entering, every time -- two lines of arithmetic, and a harder gate than the trend-maturity checks because it produces a NUMBER rather than a judgement.
CONTRIBUTION_2_late_entry_detector_quote.the_pairing: The clause cost a real trade AND declining today is still correct. A missed entry is recovered by fixing the clause for the next break, never by taking the same trade 1.70 points worse -- that reflex is how a process improvement turns into a chase. Both halves are the same discipline.

CONTRIBUTION_1_tactical_stop_is_smaller_.the_finding: TACTICAL IS AN INTRA-SESSION CONSTRUCT. On a delta-0.44 short-dated SPY contract both TACTICAL exits (+20% and -30%) sit inside ONE MEDIAN OVERNIGHT GAP and well inside one median weekend gap. Across a close, the outcome is decided by the gap and NEITHER exit level is enforceable -- the desk does not run while the market is shut. A held-over scalp is therefore not a stop-managed trade; it is an unmanaged bet whose typical move exceeds both of its own exit levels.
CONTRIBUTION_1_tactical_stop_is_smaller_.read_it_SYMMETRICALLY_this_is_not_a_bear: The gap is |absolute| and direction is close to a coin flip, so it delivers the +20% target about as often as the -30% stop. The claim is NOT 'holding overnight loses money'. It is that holding overnight REPLACES the track's risk control with a coin flip of larger magnitude than either exit. That is a governance objection, not a market call, and it would be equally true in a tape the desk liked.
CONTRIBUTION_1_tactical_stop_is_smaller_.what_the_v8_wording_actually_licenses: TACTICAL reads 'hold: hours to ~2 sessions' with a HARD TIME STOP 'flat by the close of the next session'. That is a MAXIMUM LIFETIME, not a plan. Read as a plan it authorises exactly the unstopped state above. The practical form: prefer TACTICAL entries taken early enough in a session that the +20-40% target is reachable BEFORE the bell, and treat an overnight carry as an accepted, named risk rather than a default -- with Friday the worst case at 1.36x the mean gap and 1.55x the frequency of a >0.5% move.
CONTRIBUTION_1_tactical_stop_is_smaller_.interaction_with_two_existing_rules: (a) The 2026-08-27 rule already bars opening a TACTICAL scalp in the final ~20 minutes because the volume clause is unreadable and 'the hard time stop then runs across an overnight gap on a position never observed in a normal tape'. That bullet asserted the overnight gap was bad; this measures HOW bad and shows the problem is not confined to the last 20 minutes -- it applies to any entry that will not resolve intraday. (b) The 2026-08-28T15:05Z late-entry detector prices the stop against the TRIGGER LEVEL; this prices the same stop against the CLOSE. Same arithmetic, two different things it can be too close to.
CONTRIBUTION_1_tactical_stop_is_smaller_.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION. There is no TACTICAL trigger on the tape to decline -- SPY has not closed a 5-minute bar above its session high -- so nothing was gated by this. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run the audit does not benefit. Also honest: n=96 Mondays is a thin sample for a p90, the two-year window contains one unusual regime, and the arithmetic is single-vehicle -- a lower-delta or longer-dated contract has a wider stop in underlying terms and is correspondingly less gap-dominated.

construction_finding_validated_from_the_.observation: Every fire in this arc until now had the same shape: the PRICE clause fired and the VOLUME clause failed (08-25 15:30Z and 17:00Z on desk-drawn boxes; 08-26 15:00Z and 15:40Z on a collapsed baseline; 08-28 14:40Z on a post-flush inflated baseline). construction_finding_validated_from_the_.why_that_is_useful: The 15:05Z run found the two halves measure different windows (price two-bar, volume one-bar) and proposed making both two-bar. That proposal was derived from a case where the asymmetry SUPPRESSED a good trade. This is the first observation of the asymmetry running the other way, and it shows the two-bar price requirement is doing real protective work: a one-bar reading of BOTH clauses would have licensed this entry on the 15:40Z bar alone, and the following six minutes of sideways chop on draining volume say it should not have.
construction_finding_validated_from_the_.conclusion: The symmetry argument is strengthened, not contradicted. Both clauses measured over the SAME two-bar window is correct in both directions -- it stops a one-bar volume spike from licensing an unconfirmed break just as it stops a one-bar volume miss from vetoing a confirmed one. This is a construction point, independent of either trade's outcome.
construction_finding_validated_from_the_.honest_scope: This changed no decision. The trade was declined on regime, magnitude and the Friday gap independently of the clause, and the price clause was going to fail on this bar regardless of how volume was windowed. A filter's construction can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade.

The arc's scoreboard through the 16:00Z run was five failed breaks against one break that worked and then round-tripped -- every single observation a BREAK, tested by asking whether participation arrived. Here participation arrived DECISIVELY (178% of local, 162% of pre-event) at a structural level, and the level HELD, on a higher low, followed by a 1.98-point bounce.
