CONTRIBUTION_1_the_arcs_first_DEFENDED_l.the_transferable_lesson: A VOLUME CLAUSE IS A PARTICIPATION FILTER, NOT A DIRECTION FILTER -- it confirms whichever side WINS and says nothing in advance about which side that will be. This is easy to miss because the clause is only ever CONSULTED while watching for a break, so its passing reads as 'the break is coming'. It is not: 411,987 shares at 716.84 is equally consistent with sellers being absorbed. The two cases are distinguishable only by what PRICE then does, which is precisely why the price clause is primary and the volume clause is secondary. A run that inherits a specified short trigger and sees the volume clause pass is at real risk of treating that as partial confirmation and lowering the price bar to meet it -- the exact 'more trades from a lower bar' failure v8 forbids. It did not happen here because the price clause is binary and was not close.

STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.claim: THE OPTIONS SLEEVE AND THE EQUITY BOOK ARE SEPARABLE IN THEIR CAPS AND NOT IN THEIR CASH. Every dollar of premium the options sleeve spends comes out of the SAME `cash` field that is the NUMERATOR of the >=45% equity-book cash floor -- so an options entry mechanically deepens the floor breach and pushes the equity book's reopening further away. No prior run has stated this, and the pinned rule does not cover it.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.why_the_pinned_rule_does_not_cover_it: CLAUDE.md pins the floor as cash / (cash + equity_value), EXCLUDING options_value, with the stated reason that the options sleeve 'must not be double-counted against the equity cash floor.' That pin is entirely about the DENOMINATOR -- it correctly stops the sleeve's VALUE from being counted as equity. It is silent on the NUMERATOR, and the sleeve's CASH DRAW is unavoidably counted there. Both facts are true at once, which is why this survived: the rule is right, and it answers a different question than the one that bites.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.quantified_at_todays_capital: Cash $1,546.96, equity $1,892.21, floor 44.9807%. Spending on options moves the floor to: $300 -> 39.723% (-5.26 pts); $500 -> 35.621% (-9.36 pts); $750 -> 29.636% (-15.34 pts); $1,000 -> 22.424% (-22.56 pts). So a SINGLE mid-band TACTICAL scalp at $500 -- entirely ordinary under THE FOUR LAWS, which permit $300-1,000 -- would take the equity book from a 0.02-point breach to a 9.4-point one, and the book could then only reopen if equity value FELL to about $1,280 (a further 32% equity drawdown) or roughly $500 of equity were sold.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.marginal_rates: At today's capital the floor costs 1.60 percentage points per $100 of OPTIONS premium and 2.91 points per $100 of EQUITY purchase. Equity buys cost ~1.8x more floor per dollar, which is intuitive -- but the point is that the options number is NOT ZERO, and the 'separate book' framing invites treating it as zero.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.what_it_does_and_does_not_change: It does NOT bar options entries: the floor governs equity sizing, and reading it as an options gate would double-count the sleeve in the opposite direction and freeze both books. What it changes is the HONEST COST at decision time -- during the Aug-Oct posture, whose entire purpose is defensive cash, an options entry should be priced as 'premium at risk PLUS N points of equity-book floor, extending the equity closure.' That belongs in the pre-trade checklist, said out loud, rather than discovered by a later run wondering why the floor never recovers.
STRUCTURAL_FINDING_options_spending_drai.GUARD_against_the_obvious_wrong_fix: The arithmetic runs backwards too, and a future run under floor pressure will notice: closing the SPY 700P hedge would add ~$532 of cash and lift the floor from 44.98% to 52.36%, instantly reopening the equity book. DO NOT. That is liquidating insurance to satisfy an accounting ratio -- the hedge is exempt from every mechanical exit precisely because its job is to be there when the ratio is not the problem, and its roll/close decision belongs to Ryan under the standing carve-out. Writing the tempting move down explicitly so it is recognised as tempting and refused, rather than re-derived as clever.

That completes the inversion pair: the 15:45Z run had volume pass decisively while price failed; this run is its exact mirror. In fifteen runs the two halves of the trigger have never both passed. THE FINDING IS NOT THE DECLINE: it is that LIGHT VOLUME *THROUGH* A LEVEL, AFTER HEAVY VOLUME *AT* IT, IS THE COMPLETION OF THE 16:15Z ABSORPTION FINDING -- the 16:00Z bar traded 162.5% of the pre-event baseline DEFENDING 716.79, the break bar traded 91.9% and the holding bar 57.6%. Sellers exhausted at the level; the break-through is drift, not distribution. AND THIS IS THE FIRST VOLUME VETO OF THE ARC THAT SURVIVES ITS OWN DENOMINATOR CORRECTION.

tactical_trigger_test.THE_FINDING_light_volume_through_a_level: The 16:15Z run established that heavy volume AT a level is as easily ABSORPTION as distribution -- it watched 716.79 tested to within 0.05 points on 178% participation and HOLD. This run supplies the other half of that sentence. The bar that DEFENDED the level (16:00Z) traded 411,987 = 155.6% of trailing-30 and 162.5% of pre-event. The bar that BROKE it traded 233,014 = 91.9% of pre-event, and the bar that held it broke traded 57.6%. Participation FELL BY 65% between the defence and the break. That is the signature of sellers who finished at the level, not of sellers arriving through it: the supply that was going to be sold got sold into the 16:00Z absorption, and what followed is drift into a vacuum. A breakdown that matters takes MORE volume to break a level than it took to defend it, not a third as much.
tactical_trigger_test.why_this_veto_is_STRONGER_than_every_pri: Because it survives its own denominator correction, and no prior volume veto in this arc did. The 2026-08-28T14:47Z finding established a fourth denominator mode: after a participated flush the TRAILING window is INFLATED by the flush's own bars, so the clause reads too STRICT and a break can be wrongly called unparticipated. That mode is live right now -- the trailing-30 of 264,698 carries the 15:55Z (324,741) and 16:00Z (411,987) flush bars, so its 88.0% reading is exactly the artifact the correction warns about. The correction says to characterise the break by the PRE-EVENT baseline, which answers 'arriving relative to NORMAL?'. AND THE PRE-EVENT BASELINE FAILS IT TOO -- 91.9% and 57.6%. Both denominators agree, in a case constructed to make them disagree. So this is not a denominator artifact and cannot be dismissed as one: participation on the break is genuinely ordinary-to-below-ordinary.
tactical_trigger_test.the_break_is_ALREADY_un-breaking: Stated because it is decisive and would be dishonest to omit. equity_book_state_FINDING.claim: At a 45.0001% cash ratio the equity book is at the Aug-Oct posture's fully-invested boundary. The correct description is NOT 'no compliant entry today' (which reads as a transient) but 'net addition is closed; entries are ROTATION-FUNDED ONLY'.
equity_book_state_FINDING.arithmetic: cash 1546.96 / (1546.96 + 1890.719046) = 45.000129%. Max compliant buy = cash - 0.45 x sum = $0.0044. To fund a $400 entry with NO sale, equity value would have to fall to $1,001.84 -- a further 47.0% drawdown. To fund it BY SELLING: S >= $400.00 exactly. Selling a dollar of stock buys back exactly a dollar of entry room, because a sale moves the numerator up and leaves the denominator unchanged.
equity_book_state_FINDING.why_this_reframes_it: A dollar-for-dollar funding rule is a ROTATION constraint, not a freeze. The book can still express any view it likes -- it simply cannot grow. That distinction has an operational consequence sixteen runs of 'max compliant buy = $0.004' never surfaced: A FIRED TAKE-PROFIT OR THESIS SELL DOES NOT MERELY BANK A GAIN, IT CREATES EXACTLY ONE ENTRY SLOT OF ITS OWN SIZE. A future run that banks PNC at its 255.50 target should immediately re-run the hunt with ~$466 of freshly compliant room, rather than logging the sale and standing down on a stale floor reading.
equity_book_state_FINDING.hypersensitivity_warning: d(ratio)/d(equity) = -cash/sum^2 = -1.309e-4 per dollar, i.e. ~1.31 floor-points per $100 of equity MARK movement and ~0.25 points per 1% move in the book. Measured live: the 16:20Z run read 44.9807% and this run reads 45.0001% -- the entire 'breach' cured on $1.49 of mark drift, with no trade. SO: NEVER report the floor as having 'recovered' or the book as having 'reopened' on a mark-drift crossing. The reading is noise at this resolution, and its improvement is mechanically identical to the book LOSING money -- the floor gets healthier precisely as the positions get worse. Both directions of that sentence are true and neither is news.

THE_FINDING_friday_theta_collapses_the_s.the_mechanism: The TACTICAL hard time stop is worded 'flat by the close of the next session' -- a fixed number of SESSIONS. Theta is charged in CALENDAR days. So the same time stop spans 3 calendar days for a Friday entry and 1 for a Tuesday entry: THE SAME RULE COSTS 3x THE THETA depending only on the weekday. On a 7-DTE vehicle that is -24.0% of premium (NVDA 09-04) to -27.4% (QQQ 09-04 712P) -- four-fifths of the way to the -30% stop, paid to the clock before the underlying moves at all.

THE_FINDING_friday_theta_collapses_the_s.relation_to_the_15:35Z_gap_finding: COMPLEMENTARY, not duplicative, and they compound. That finding measured the weekend GAP (median 0.342% on SPY, exceeding the whole stop distance) -- a symmetric, direction-neutral risk. This one measures the weekend THETA -- an asymmetric, certain COST paid in one direction only. A Friday TACTICAL carry bears both: a certain -24% drag plus a coin-flip larger than what remains of the stop.
THE_FINDING_friday_theta_collapses_the_s.honest_scope: It changed no decision on the day it was found -- the trade was already declined on the incomplete price clause before this arithmetic was run, so nothing was licensed or vetoed by it. That is the only condition under which the desk's own gates can be audited credibly. Single-vehicle arithmetic on one Friday; a lower-delta or longer-dated contract has a wider stop in underlying terms and is correspondingly less theta-dominated. THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.claim: THE TWO-BAR CONFIRMATION REQUIREMENT AND THE 15-MINUTE RUN CADENCE ARE ADDITIVE LATENCIES, AND THEIR SUM IS COMPARABLE TO THE ENTIRE DURATION OF THE MOVE A TACTICAL SCALP EXISTS TO CAPTURE. Measured on the one break of this arc that passed every filter.
THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.the_numbers: The break move ran from the 219.760 trigger (17:00Z bar open) to the 217.890 session low (17:10Z bar) in TEN MINUTES. The price clause cannot confirm before the second 5-minute bar closes = TEN MINUTES minimum, here completing at 17:09:59Z. This run was fired at 17:15Z and had a live option quote at 17:18:01Z -- 5 to 8 minutes after confirmation, 18 minutes after the trigger. THE CLAUSE CONFIRMED AT THE EXTREMUM OF THE MOVE, TO WITHIN ONE BAR.
THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.why_this_reframes_the_drought: Eighteen runs, no options entry, and the standing explanation has been setup quality. That explanation is incomplete. This setup was not marginal: structural level, both clauses passing against both denominators, defence-vs-break ratio 1.98x confirming, a 1.07%-of-mid chain with 14,613 OI, the stop 2.22 points clear of the trigger, and a target sitting on the 20-day SMA. It was UNREACHABLE, not poor. Some fraction of the drought is arrival time, not judgment.
THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.what_it_does_NOT_license: It is NOT an argument to enter on the break bar without the holding bar. Five of the six prior breaks in this arc failed, and the two-bar clause is what caught them; relaxing it to buy back the lost minutes is the exact loosening the 08-25/08-26 tuning arc forbids, and it would convert a latency problem into a losses problem. It is also NOT an argument to widen the volume or liquidity gates.
THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.the_strategic_consequence_for_Ryan: A desk that fires every 15 minutes can reliably participate in setups whose ENTRY WINDOW is measured in hours, and cannot reliably participate in ones measured in minutes. Bar-confirmed intraday BREAKOUT scalps are in the second category whenever the move is shorter than confirmation-plus-arrival. The tracks that fit the cadence are CORE swings and mean-reversion AT a level (where the level itself is the entry and it waits for you) rather than breakouts THROUGH one (where the entry is a moving target that leaves without you). Worth him knowing because the trigger cadence is his to change, not the desk's -- and because it is the honest answer to 'why so few trades'.
THE_FINDING_confirmation_latency_vs_run_.falsifiable: If a future TACTICAL break is captured cleanly, the mechanism is wrong or the move was slow enough. Record the trigger-to-extremum duration on every fire from now on; the prediction is that fires whose move completes inside ~15 minutes will be systematically unreachable and ones that grind for 30+ minutes will be reachable.

Mark such a crossing 'provisional' and require it to hold across sessions. THE_RETRACE_GATE.the_arithmetic: retrace_pct = (current - break_extreme) / (trigger - break_extreme). Compute it AT THE MOMENT OF ENTRY, not at the moment of the trigger. the_finding.claim: A BREAKOUT HAS THREE OUTCOMES -- EXTEND, FAIL, STALL -- AND THE RETRACE GATE ONLY ENCODES TWO. Built on price distance alone, it reads STALL as PASS, and because the reading is an instantaneous price against two fixed levels it oscillates across its own threshold at the noise frequency of a range-bound tape.
the_finding.measured_retrace_oscillation: NVDA, trigger = the 219.760 session low, extremum = 217.890 (17:10Z bar). Retrace = (current - extremum) / (trigger - extremum), on 1-minute closes 17:11-17:30Z: 20.9, 34.5, 36.4, 43.6, 45.5, 54.0, 69.8, 55.1, 63.6, 45.7, 44.4, 36.9, 41.4, 43.3, 39.0, 36.6, 44.4, 59.4, 42.8, 39.3 percent. FOUR CROSSINGS of the 50% line in twenty minutes; full range 20.9%-69.8%. The 17:15Z run measured 76.5% and declined as a CHASE; this run at 17:31Z measures 42.8% and would PASS. NOTHING HAPPENED IN BETWEEN -- no new trigger, no new extremum, no new participation. Which side of the gate a run lands on is decided by its arrival minute.
the_finding.the_volume_half_is_monotonic_over_the_id: Break bar 17:00Z 2,156,679, then 1,393,130 / 1,508,782 / 1,073,106 / 800,242 / 712,021. The latest bar is 33.0% of the break bar -- a 67.0% decay -- and, decisively, 77.9% of the PRE-BREAK trailing-30 baseline (914,303 over 16:30-16:55Z). Participation did not merely fail to build on the break; it has drained BELOW the rate that prevailed before the break happened. Where the price gate flickers, the participation reading is unambiguous and points one way for six consecutive bars.
the_finding.feed_integrity_checked_first: All six 5-minute buckets reconciled against their 1-minute sums per the 2026-08-28 direction rule: +2.02%, +1.26%, +2.99%, +1.08%, +1.71%, +1.85%. Every one inside tolerance and every one on the BUCKET-ABOVE side, so no hole propagated into either the decay series or the baseline. The decay is real, not an artifact -- which matters because a holed bucket would have depressed exactly the denominator this finding rests on.
the_finding.the_fix: Add the third state explicitly, and source it from PARTICIPATION rather than from price. A confirmed break is EXTENDING only while it is still making new extremes or still trading at or above its break-bar rate; it is FAILING once the retrace gate trips on completed bars; and it is STALLED when neither holds -- no new extremum for N bars AND participation back at or below the pre-break baseline. STALL IS A DECLINE, and it is the state the binary gate cannot express. Evaluate on COMPLETED bars, never on the instantaneous print, so the reading cannot flicker between two runs that see the same tape.
the_finding.why_this_is_not_re_tuning_the_filter: The 2026-08-26 arc capstone forbids answering a failed break by tuning the measurement, and this is deliberately NOT that. The threshold is untouched at 50%; the level is untouched; the confirmation clause is untouched. What is added is a STATE the gate had no way to represent -- and it is added because the gate's FIRST live application returned PASS on a break the desk would obviously decline, which is a construction defect visible without reference to any outcome. the_measurement.the_controls_which_are_what_make_it_a_fi: The obvious objection -- front boards are simply always richer -- is refuted by measuring names where the answer is known. SPY at strike 770: front 0.100806 vs back 0.115484, kink 0.8729, i.e. the front board is CHEAPER, ordinary contango. the_measurement.solving_the_two_boards: Variance is additive in time and the event's variance is the same absolute quantity on every board spanning it, so base_vol^2 = (var_back - var_front)/((T2-T1)/365) and V_event = var_front - base_vol^2*(T1/365). AVGO: base vol 38.12%, implied 1-day event move +/-8.74%. NVDA: base vol 32.27%, residual event +/-2.09% -- correctly near-nothing for a print that already happened. SPY: base vol 12.00%, V_event NEGATIVE at -0.0000812, i.e. the method returns 'no event' rather than a small false positive. That negative control is the strongest evidence it is measuring an event and not fitting noise.
the_measurement.the_second_and_separate_defect: AVGO's ex-gap IV/RV ratio climbed monotonically over seven sessions -- 1.3371, 1.4115, 1.4190, 1.4041, 1.4463, 1.4743, 1.4940 -- and 1.494 is the richest reading in this file. The ratio rose because AVGO got QUIETER, not because its options got dearer -- and those two readings license opposite trades from an identical headline number.
the_measurement.transferable: Same defect as this file's entire volume-denominator arc, arriving in the IV instrument where nobody had looked. A ratio has two moving parts and its headline cannot tell you which one moved. The 2026-08-27 finding stated this for FORECASTING a ratio; it applies with equal force to READING one. Rule: never cite an IV/RV ratio as evidence without stating which leg moved -- it is two divisions.

entries.the_transferable_lesson: AN 'OVER-DETERMINED' CLOSURE IS THE MOST DANGEROUS KIND TO INHERIT, AND ITS REDUNDANCY IS EXACTLY WHY. A verdict resting on two independent reasons reads as robust -- belt and braces, safe to trust. But each reason carries its own expiry, and they expire by DIFFERENT mechanisms on DIFFERENT clocks: the floor died by a commit to master, the throttle dies by the clock striking a new trading day. Neither expiry is visible in the key that cites them, and a reader checking one surviving reason concludes the verdict still stands. So redundancy at the moment of writing converts into a verdict that outlives BOTH its grounds while still looking well-supported. DETECTOR: when a conclusion is recorded as over-determined, write each reason's EXPIRY CONDITION next to it, not just the reason. A reason without an expiry is indistinguishable from a permanent one. This is the same family as the file's recurring 'a check that passes for the wrong reason' -- here arriving as a conclusion that survives for reasons that have themselves quietly died.

durable_finding.measurement: trade_journal.json holds 684 entries spanning 2026-08-11T16:55Z -> 2026-08-29T12:18Z (17 days, 5.35 MB). 146 entries carry no run_type. Their date distribution is entirely PRE-RULE: 08-11 (17), 08-12 (33), 08-13 (38), 08-14 (38), 08-15 (1), 08-16 (1), 08-17 (1), 08-18 (14), 08-19 (1), 08-20 (2). durable_finding.why_no_repair_was_made: The CLAUDE.md text calls a missing run_type 'a defect to repair, not to skip past', and a careless reading of that would have this run rewrite 146 historical records. It should not, for two reasons. (1) The prescribed filter ALREADY handles them correctly: rule (2) says cadence/health/rate math counts ONLY scheduler-fired types, and an ABSENT field is not in that allow-list, so it is excluded by construction. The 2026-08-21 incident being guarded against was the opposite error -- a run COUNTING live-user entries as scheduler fires -- which a missing field cannot cause. (2) Retroactively INFERRING a run_type for a 9-to-18-day-old entry is guesswork, and a wrong label is strictly worse than an absent one: it converts a record the filter safely drops into one the filter silently counts, in the exact direction (making a dead trigger look healthy) that the rule exists to prevent.
durable_finding.transferable_lesson: Same class as the 2026-08-17 journal-rotation flag, and the same corrective: MEASURE AN INHERITED FLAG BEFORE REMEDIATING IT. Both flags named a real observation and implied a fix the data does not support -- rotation would have archived zero entries at a 30-day cutoff, and this repair would have degraded a filter that already works. A defect whose occurrences all predate the rule that forbids it is EVIDENCE THE RULE IS WORKING, not an open wound. Record the boundary so the next instance recognises the residue instead of re-litigating it.
durable_finding.when_a_repair_WOULD_be_right: If any entry dated 2026-08-21 or later is ever found without run_type, that IS a live rule breach: repair that entry at source in the run that wrote it, and treat it as a process failure. Historical pre-rule residue stays as it is.

finding_journal_noop_bloat.title: THE POST-CLOSE PROTOCOL IS OBEYED IN LETTER AND BROKEN IN SUBSTANCE: 44 WEEKEND NO-OP ENTRIES AVERAGING 6.8 KB, AGAINST A PROTOCOL THAT SAYS 'A NO-OP LOGGED IN A FEW LINES IS THE CORRECT OUTPUT'.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.measurement: Entries with trading_day_et 2026-08-28 and run_type post_close_overnight: 44 entries, 292.3 KB, mean 6,802 bytes. Their prompt_version fields alone total 22.0 KB (mean 512) restating one staleness already tracked in a flag and in CLAUDE.md. File is now 5,427.8 KB, up from 1.09 MB on 2026-08-17. Every one of those runs correctly placed no trade, rolled no artifact and reconciled cleanly -- then wrote a full-length entry re-deriving the same four facts.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.mechanism: CLAUDE.md's '_note grows a paragraph every run' failure, one container to the left. Fixed at the per-position level (overwrite _current_state), it re-appeared at the top-level-key level (the eleven _SESSION keys of 2026-08-25) and has now re-appeared in the JOURNAL -- hardest to see here because each entry is individually well-written and individually justified. A run inherits the prior entry's shape and matches it; matching a 6.8 KB no-op produces another. Nobody appends junk; everybody is thorough about nothing.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.cost: Not disk. (a) Context per run -- the cost the 2026-08-17 finding named, now 5x worse. (b) Signal -- 44 near-identical entries make the ONE post-close run that finds something real indistinguishable from the 43 that did not.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.what_NOT_to_do: Do NOT rotate or archive. The 2026-08-17 finding measured that trap and it still holds: the file spans 2026-08-11..2026-08-30, ~19 days, so a 30-day cutoff still moves ZERO entries; and the market-hours grades_considered entries are the desk's memory.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.the_fix: On a redundant post-close/weekend run write the short entry the protocol already prescribes -- headline, reconciliation, artifacts-not-rolled, flags-untouched. POINT to a tracked flag in one line instead of restating it. Do not re-derive the regime, re-poll quotes, or re-explain a rule the next run can read itself.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.honest_scope: This entry is 5.2 KB against the 6.8 KB mean -- better, not exemplary, and most of the gap is this finding itself, which is one-off content the next run should NOT reproduce. The test is the next few weekend entries, which should be ~1-2 KB. An earlier draft of this entry claimed 'roughly a third the size'; that was false against its own measurement and was corrected before commit. A finding about padding that pads is self-refuting.
finding_journal_noop_bloat.detector: If your post-close entry is longer than the prior run's and neither the broker nor master changed, you are padding. The honest length of a no-op is short.

entries.finding_hole_corrupted_the_price_clause: A three-symbol feed hole at the 14:10Z 5-minute bucket -- NVDA reported 87,672 vs a 1,057,298 one-minute sum (-91.71%), SPY 6,907 vs 120,938 (-94.29%), QQQ 17,436 vs 138,954 (-87.45%) -- the cross-symbol agreement signature from 2026-08-27, and by the 2026-08-28 DIRECTION rule the BUCKET is the holed side in every case. THE NEW PART IS THAT IT CORRUPTED PRICE, IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION. NVDA's holed bucket reported a LOW of 220.000; the true low rebuilt from its one-minute constituents is 219.267, which sits BELOW the 219.6195 level the break was made through. The 5-minute series therefore showed price consolidating tightly above the level when it had in fact broken, traded back UNDER the level mid-bucket, and only reclaimed 220 in the final minute. A run reading the 5-minute series alone scores 'held beyond the level' as satisfied; it was not. This file already knows holes hide session extremes and depress volume denominators -- what is new is that the hidden extreme can be the TRIGGER LEVEL itself, and that on an upside break the surviving constituent minute is disproportionately the highest one, so the bias is toward false positives on exactly the bars a breakout desk cares about. RULE: reconcile the bucket against the one-minute series before testing the PRICE clause, not only before computing a volume baseline. Also a MIXED presentation worth noting -- the OHLC is byte-for-byte the 14:14 minute (single-constituent signature) while the volume matches no constituent minute at all (partial form), so neither signature alone is the test; the reconciliation GAP remains the test.
entries.finding_reserve_is_stricter_of_two: Every run since the 2026-08-29 capital amendment has computed deployable capital as unleveraged_buying_power minus a 5%-of-total operational reserve, and none has applied FOUR LAWS #4's flat '>=$250 unencumbered', which is STRICTER at this account size. 0.05 x $3,973.02 = $198.65 < $250, so the binding reserve is $250 and deployable is $796.96, not the $848.45 the 14:05Z and 14:15Z runs quoted -- a $51.35 overstatement. The two rules agree only at a total_value of $5,000; BELOW that the flat $250 binds, and this account has been below $5,000 for the entire life of the full-deployment policy, so the 5% figure has been wrong every time it has been quoted and stays wrong until the account grows ~26%. It survived because the 5% formula is the NEW rule written with emphasis, and applying it feels like compliance, while the $250 sits as one sentence inside a longer law about margin that a run reads for 'is unleveraged_buying_power the budget?', answers yes, and leaves. DETECTOR: reserve = max(0.05 * total_value, 250.00), one line, computed every run. IMMATERIAL TODAY -- no trade was placed and both figures cover anything contemplated -- but material the moment cash sits between the two numbers, where it would authorise an entry FOUR LAWS #4 forbids, and the FOUR LAWS admit no thesis.

finding_nvda_break_resolved.what_the_handoff_asked: The 14:20Z run declined the NVDA break of its 219.6195 session high on an INCOMPLETE two-bar price clause (the holding bar was still open) and named three conditions for the setup to become live: a completed close above the level with the next bar holding above it, participation over that two-bar window clearing the then-current baselines, and SPY/QQQ ceasing to make session lows. finding_nvda_break_resolved.price_clause_COMPLETED_and_it_did_not_he: It passed, then decayed. Bucket closes: 14:10 = 220.190 and 14:15 = 220.000, BOTH above 219.6195, so the two-bar clause was satisfied as of 14:19Z. But 14:20 closed 219.550 -- BELOW the level on a completed close -- and 14:25 closed 220.075, reclaiming it. NVDA has now crossed the trigger level in both directions three times in twenty minutes. Twenty-five minutes after the break it sits at 220.065, +0.45 (+0.20%) above the trigger and BELOW its 220.360 session high. The level became a chop zone, not support.
finding_nvda_break_resolved.the_new_part_worth_keeping: This is the first fire in the whole break arc where the two-bar price clause COMPLETED and the level was then LOST on a later completed close before being reclaimed. The clause as written is a two-bar test and is silent about what happens on bar three. It is not wrong -- a filter has to stop looking somewhere -- but it means a SATISFIED price clause is a necessary condition that expires, not a state that persists. Do not carry 'the price clause passed' forward from an earlier run as though it were still true; re-test it on the current bars, exactly as the 2026-08-25 stale-box finding requires for the numbers inside the clause.
finding_nvda_break_resolved.volume_clause_FAILS_on_both_denominators: Feed reconciled first per the 2026-08-28 direction rule. Two-bar window per the 2026-08-28 construction fix: break bar 1,081,849, holding bar 1,185,159. Trailing-30 baseline (six buckets 13:40-14:09) = 1,157,093 -> 93.5% and 102.4%. Session bucket rate (twelve buckets, corrected) = 1,305,606 -> 82.9% and 90.8%. Confirmation requires at-or-above the trailing local mean AND not materially below the session rate: the break bar fails the first and BOTH fail the second. NOT CONFIRMED. Note honestly that no post-first-hour baseline exists yet -- the first hour ended at 14:30Z and exactly one bucket has printed since -- so the trailing-30 denominator is still the inflated too-strict mode from 2026-08-25, and the clause is being read at its most conservative. At 14:18Z: bid 5.05 / ask 5.10, mid 5.075, spread 0.99% of mid, delta 0.5265, $507.50, NVDA 220.17. At 14:32:28Z: bid 4.90 / ask 5.00, mid 4.950, spread 2.02% of mid, delta 0.518951, theta -0.226292/day, IV 0.313893, OI 10,902, vol 4,715, $495.00, NVDA 220.065. finding_late_entry_cost_on_a_flat_underl.what_it_says: Delta explains about -0.055 of the -0.125 and theta about -0.002 over fourteen minutes. Roughly half the loss is neither: it is implied-vol bleed plus a bid/ask that DOUBLED from 0.99% to 2.02% of mid. So an 11-DTE ATM tactical vehicle costs on the order of 1.2-1.4% of premium per quarter-hour to hold with the underlying standing still -- against a +20% target that needs only ~+1.04% on NVDA. The trade must work NOW; 'why NOW' is not a stylistic gate, it is the arithmetic.

concurrent_run_union.CROSS_VALIDATION_not_conflict: The two runs reached the SAME verdict on the SAME setup independently and by different routes -- the sibling's headline is 'NVDA break's price clause passed and it failed anyway', which is this run's finding_nvda_break_resolved arrived at separately. Both resolutions are preserved side by side inside _NVDA_BREAK_DECLINED_ON_TAPE_NOT_VEHICLE rather than one overwriting the other. Note the sibling graded the volume clause MARGINALLY PASSED where this run grades it FAILED: the difference is the denominator, not the data -- this run tested against BOTH the trailing-30 and the session bucket rate per the 2026-08-26 dual-denominator rule and the session-rate leg fails. Recorded as a genuine disagreement, not smoothed over.
concurrent_run_union.NEAR_MISS_WORTH_KEEPING_a_lossy_dedup_ke: The first attempt at this union deduped entries on (run_utc, run_type, headline[:60]) and produced 737 entries from two 740-entry sides -- it DELETED three pre-existing records. Cause: trade_journal.json already contains legitimate same-(run_utc, run_type) pairs from EARLIER concurrent-run collisions, so the very condition this merge exists to handle is the condition that makes a natural-looking dedup key lossy. A second attempt, deduping on exact content, then double-counted the shared base because one Counter was consumed by the first side before the second was tested. The version that shipped avoids the class entirely: take the other side's file as-is and APPEND only this run's own entry, then assert the tail is exactly [their run_utc, my run_utc] and that git diff --stat shows insertions only. DETECTOR, and it is the same one this file already prescribes for serialization: trust the stat line, not the merge logic -- a union that DELETES lines is wrong by construction, whatever the code looked like. Caught before commit; nothing was pushed in the broken state.

finding_oversold_cohort_relative_strengt.claim: MEASURE THE REPORT'S OVERSOLD LIST AS A COHORT BEFORE GRADING ITS MEMBERS ONE AT A TIME. On 2026-08-31 the 15 non-held RSI2 / oversold-uptrend candidates averaged -1.4524% against SPY's -0.4497%; 14 of 15 underperformed the index and exactly ONE was green. An RSI2 mean-reversion entry is a bet that an oversold name STOPS going down; a cohort being distributed 3.2x the index is the trend-maturity gate's clause (c) firing on the whole class at once.
finding_oversold_cohort_relative_strengt.the_honest_caveat_which_limits_the_claim: An oversold cohort underperforming on a down day is PARTLY EXPECTED BY CONSTRUCTION -- the screen selects for names already being sold, which skews the sample toward weakness and high beta. So this does NOT prove the setup class is broken, and a run that reads it that way has over-claimed. What it does establish is narrower and sufficient: today shows DISTRIBUTION, not STABILIZATION, and stabilization is the thing the entry is buying. Note the cohort is not merely high-beta either -- GD, RTX, CAT and MAR are low-beta names and all four fell 1.2-2.3% against an index down 0.45%.
finding_oversold_cohort_relative_strengt.what_it_changes_in_practice: Compute the cohort number FIRST, then grade individuals. It costs one get_equity_quotes call, it is available before any thesis workup, and it tells you whether you are looking for a stabilizing name inside a stabilizing group or hunting the single exception. Nine runs of this session graded names one at a time and reached the same answer nine times.
finding_oversold_cohort_relative_strengt.the_exception_and_why_it_still_failed: REGN was the one green name -- a 1-in-15 relative-strength outlier, which is precisely the stabilization signature the setup wants. finding_reachability_has_a_direction.the_class: This is the file's most-repeated shape -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving in an AVAILABILITY test rather than a confirmation clause. finding_block_print_denominator.what: XLF 16:20Z 5-minute bucket 488,442 against neighbours 28,336 and 30,927. 1-minute sum for 16:20-16:24 = 8,755 + 388,683 + 22,018 + 38,643 + 30,343 = 488,442 -- EXACT to the share, so the 2026-08-28 direction rule reports clean in both directions. The spike is one minute: 16:21Z, 388,683 shares, 44.4x and 17.7x its neighbours, price range 57.735/57.725 = 0.010 points = 0.017%.
finding_block_print_denominator.effect: Trailing-30 baseline over the six 16:00-16:25Z buckets reads RAW 108,766 vs BLOCK-ADJUSTED 43,986 -- 2.47x. The confirmation clause runs ~2.5x too strict for the next half hour, set by a print that moved price one cent.
finding_block_print_denominator.why_no_detector_catches_it: The feed-integrity family is built to catch MISSING volume. Excess volume is not an error, so reconciliation passes and the denominator is still wrong. The four prior denominator modes are all about which WINDOW the baseline covers; this one is about a single bar inside a correct window.
finding_block_print_denominator.detector: A 1-minute bar that is a large multiple of BOTH neighbours WITH NEAR-ZERO RANGE is a block cross, not participation -- exclude it from any confirmation denominator. Mirror of the existing 'tiny fraction of both neighbours is provisional' rule. The discriminator is RANGE: participation moves price, a cross does not.
finding_block_print_denominator.dangerous_case: Errs STRICT here, the safe direction. The hazard is the same print landing ON the break bar, where it would manufacture the confirmation the clause exists to withhold. Check the break bar's range against its volume before crediting it.
finding_block_print_denominator.honest_scope: Changed no decision. XLF is not a TACTICAL vehicle at this size and no trigger existed anywhere; SPY's own 16:20Z bucket reconciled clean at +4.13%. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run the audit does not benefit.

finding_complex_veto_needs_dispersion.rule: A complex veto needs BOTH a magnitude test and a DISPERSION test. Quote the members and the best-to-worst spread; if one member is a multi-sigma outlier or any member is GREEN, the ETF number is a weighted average and not a regime. Magnitude alone cannot distinguish a de-rating complex from a complex containing one blowup -- both print the same ETF number.
finding_complex_veto_needs_dispersion.why_it_is_the_dangerous_half: The 16:16Z test was written precisely to stop a correct veto being reused by analogy, and it did catch the financials and power-complex over-extensions. finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.status: DURABLE ledger-mechanics rule. Not session-scoped. Same family as the `git diff --stat` rule: trust the assertion, not the enumerated procedure.
finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.claim: The CONCURRENT-RUN COLLISION rule says to resolve a trade_journal.json conflict as a UNION -- 'keep both entries, ordered by run_utc' -- and NEVER specifies the DEDUP KEY. A natural-looking key silently DELETES legitimate records, and the deletion is invisible because the merged file still parses, still sorts, and still contains today's work.
finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.measured: Resolving the 17:15Z/17:20Z collision live. Base HEAD~1 = 753 entries; mine 754 (base + my 17:20Z); sibling 754 (base + its 17:15Z); correct union = 755. Keying the dedup on (run_utc, headline[:60]) returned 751 -- FOUR entries short of the base file, i.e. it destroyed history that neither side had touched. Cause: this journal contains multiple entries sharing a run_utc AND a headline prefix, written by earlier concurrent same-slot runs -- exactly the collisions this union rule exists to preserve. The rule's own output is what breaks its naive implementation.
finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.why_it_is_invisible: A count is not a check. 751 looks like a plausible number, the file is valid JSON, entries sort correctly, and both runs' current entries ARE present -- so every surface inspection passes. Only comparing the SETS reveals the loss. This is the file's most-repeated defect (a check that passes for the wrong reason) arriving in the merge tooling rather than in a trading decision.
finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.the_rule: Dedup on the FULL serialized entry (json.dumps(e, sort_keys=True)), never on a field subset -- two genuinely identical entries are safe to collapse, two entries differing anywhere are not. Then ASSERT set containment before writing: every entry from BOTH sides must appear in the merged set. Three lines, and they catch every variant including the ones not listed here. SECOND HALF, found the same minute by re-checking the diff: 'ordered by run_utc' must mean APPEND-IN-ORDER, not RE-SORT. This journal is NOT strictly sorted -- five historical pairs are inverted, written out of order by earlier concurrent same-slot runs -- so a global sort silently REWRITES five positions of history that neither side touched, turning a 40-line append into a 360-line diff. Preserve the incoming file's order verbatim and append; let the `git diff --stat` rule be the detector, exactly as it is for serialization mismatches.
finding_union_merge_needs_a_dedup_key.honest_scope: Caught before the write, so no history was lost and no decision changed. Recorded because the wrong key produced a merged file that would have passed review, and because the union rule has been invoked repeatedly (precedent PR #210) without ever naming the key.

measurement_bug_caught_and_corrected.claim: AN ENTRY-DAY HIGH THAT PRECEDED THE FILL INFLATED PNC'S BEST EXCURSION BY 6x AND ITS PROGRESS-TO-TARGET BY MORE THAN 6x. The first pass of this audit included each entry day's full high/low range. For PNC that read MFE +3.43% and 'best excursion covered 93.7% of the distance to target' -- a number that would have supported the OPPOSITE conclusion, i.e. that the position had nearly worked and merely gave it back.
measurement_bug_caught_and_corrected.the_mechanism: PNC's ledger entry price is 246.4729 and the 08-19 daily CLOSE is 246.46 -- a 0.005% difference, so the fill was at the close. That same session opened at 254.49 and fell all day. The 254.93 high therefore occurred BEFORE the position existed. Corrected by measuring from the first bar that could contain the fill: MFE +0.56% (the 08-20 high of 247.86), progress to target 15.4%.
measurement_bug_caught_and_corrected.the_general_rule: A daily bar is not a position's bar. On the ENTRY day the position exists for only part of the session, so the day's high/low bound the STOCK, not the trade -- and the error is directional whenever the entry is a mean-reversion buy, because those fill near the day's LOW after a decline, making the pre-entry high systematically flattering. Before using any entry-day extreme, compare the fill price to that day's open and close: a fill at the close means the whole day's range is pre-entry. Where fill timing is known (MDLZ 13:40:03Z, ROST 13:37:13Z, MMM 13:37:54Z -- all near the open) the entry-day range is legitimately usable.
measurement_bug_caught_and_corrected.why_it_belongs_in_the_file: Same family as the affordability-tier bug (spot price / ATM strike / wrong expiry board / modelled estimate) and the denominator bugs: a number was taken from a convenient source that was never the thing being asked about, nothing errored, and the wrong reading was indistinguishable from the right one. It is the first instance of that family aimed at the desk's OWN P/L rather than at a market input, which is where it would be least likely to be double-checked.

finding_TENTH_VOID_FLOOR_INSTANCE_and_th.why_it_matters_more_than_instances_8_and: Those sat in reference documents. finding_TENTH_VOID_FLOOR_INSTANCE_and_th.why_nine_sweeps_missed_it_THE_NEW_AXIS: Not the corpus and not the constant -- both of those dimensions were already correct here. holdings.json is named as SWEPT in this key's own corpus list, and both retired constants were eventually searched. The miss was on a THIRD axis: ENCODING. Every recorded query was PROSE ('0.45', '45%', 'cash floor', 'compliant buy', 'book is closed'). This copy encodes the floor as JSON NUMBERS in FIELD NAMES plus a status string in different capitalisation and without the copula. Grep '45%' does not match 45.0; grep 'book is closed' does not match 'BOOK CLOSED'; grep 'cash floor' does not match 'cash_floor_pct'. Every single query was constructed to miss it.
finding_TENTH_VOID_FLOOR_INSTANCE_and_th.transferable_lesson: A repeal has THREE dimensions, not the two this key previously named: every FILE asserting current state, every CONSTANT retired, and every ENCODING those constants can take -- prose, bare numeral, FIELD NAME, and a status string in any capitalisation. A structured artifact does not spell its rules the way a document does, so a prose sweep is systematically blind to precisely the machine-readable copies a machine will act on. Practical form: grep the SCHEMA (field names containing floor/cap/min/max/compliant) and the bare numeral alongside the prose, and in a JSON artifact ENUMERATE THE TOP-LEVEL KEYS rather than trusting full-text search.
finding_TENTH_VOID_FLOOR_INSTANCE_and_th.meta_lesson_and_the_reason_no_completion: This key has now declared the sweep complete THREE times -- at seven instances, at nine, and it was wrong both times; the pattern is that each sweep widens the query along whichever axis the LAST failure exposed, then declares victory. RSI2 peaked 08-26 at 66.05 (3.95 short of the >=70 trigger) and that session's HIGH was 246.425, four point eight CENTS below the 246.4729 entry. finding_rsi2_reversion_and_profit_need_n.vindicates_the_08_26_gate_at_near_zero_c: The 2026-08-26 finding gated the RSI2>=70 mechanical exit on price > entry after it fired on this very name at 78.5 intraday while 0.34% underwater. This measurement is the follow-through: across the ENTIRE cycle the best available exit was +$0.6071/sh on an intraday high (+$1.11 on the position, before spread) and the best CLOSE was -0.73%. The gate prevented a realized loss and forfeited essentially nothing. A gate is best evidenced when its opportunity cost is measured, not assumed.
finding_rsi2_reversion_and_profit_need_n.mechanism: RSI2 is a relative oscillator normalized to recent range, so it re-baselines to wherever price settles. An entry taken before price bottoms means the whole reversion is measured off a LOWER base: the oscillator traverses its full range while price merely chops. PNC went 1.6 -> 66 without ever leaving a 241.30-247.08 band. 'The signal reverted' and 'the trade is profitable' are therefore independent events.
finding_rsi2_reversion_and_profit_need_n.honest_scope: n=1 name, one cycle. report_duty_collision_resolved_by_DISCAR.why_discard_and_not_union: The union rule exists to preserve SEPARABLE WORK, not to preserve both containers. report_duty_collision_resolved_by_DISCAR.the_transferable_part: A collision is resolved by asking WHAT IS SEPARABLE, not by defaulting to union. Union was right on 2026-08-28 because each report carried a measurement the other lacked. finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.claim: Today's closing-flow boundary is 19:35Z -- TWENTY-FIVE minutes before the bell, not the forty measured on 2026-08-28. Had either session's number been adopted as a constant it would have been wrong on the other, in opposite directions.
finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.feed_integrity_first: Every post-19:20Z SPY 5-minute bucket reconciled against its 1-minute sum before any ratio was computed, per the 2026-08-28 direction rule. 19:20Z +3.3% / 19:25Z +0.4% / 19:30Z -2.7% CLEAN; 19:35Z -10.7% and 19:40Z -40.2% are BUCKET-HOLED (bucket materially BELOW its 1-minute sum), so the 1-minute sums 199,211 and 211,690 substitute. Using the raw buckets would have understated the ramp and hidden the boundary entirely -- the holed direction here is the one that manufactures a false 'no ramp' reading.
finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.why_the_19:30Z_run_saw_nothing: Its window ended before the boundary. The first three post-19:20Z buckets run 0.78x / 0.95x / 0.94x -- at or BELOW the prevailing rate -- so a run measuring at 19:30Z correctly observes no ramp and incorrectly concludes the phenomenon did not occur. The transferable point: a NEGATIVE result about a closing-window effect is only meaningful if the measurement window actually reaches the bell. 'Did not reproduce' measured at 19:30Z is under-determined, not false.
finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.corrects_a_stated_bound_of_the_08_28_fin: That finding offered month-end rebalancing flow as the reason its ramp might be unusually wide (a Friday two sessions from month-end). TODAY IS MONTH-END ITSELF -- the last trading day of August, the canonical rebalance-flow session -- and its ramp is roughly HALF as wide (1.159x vs 2.081x) and starts fifteen minutes later. So month-end flow does not explain the 08-28 width; that hypothesis is weakened by the one session best placed to confirm it.
finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.second_order_observation: The 19:42Z one-minute bar printed 1,778 shares between neighbours of 52,740 and 87,850 -- the 1-minute hole signature. So the 19:40Z bucket's substituted 211,690 is a LOWER BOUND and the true ramp is slightly wider than stated. Both sides of the feed were holed inside one window, which is the first time this desk has recorded that; it does not change the boundary.
finding_closing_ramp_boundary_is_per_ses.honest_scope: CHANGED NO DECISION. TACTICAL was already barred this run on the closing window and the overnight-carry arithmetic, and no trigger fired in either index all session. A filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run the audit does not benefit. n=2 sessions is still thin -- the rule remains DETECT PER SESSION, and two differing boundaries are the argument for that rule, not the start of a new constant.

finding.summary: All four autonomous equity entries ever placed (ROST, MDLZ, MMM, GD) filled 13:36-13:40Z, i.e. 6-10 minutes after the bell. In 4 of 4 a better price printed within the following 30 minutes: 0.761% / 0.463% / 0.500% / 1.076%, mean 0.700% (~$3.50 per $500 entry, ~$14 total). Mean fill percentile 73.6% of the session's eventual range, with 3 of 4 in the top ~16%.
finding.mechanism: The signal fights the execution. The entry comes from an RSI2 MEAN-REVERSION screen computed on the PREVIOUS session's close (the fresh report does not land until ~14:15Z), and the opening ten minutes is exactly when yesterday's oversold names get their reflexive bounce. The run buys the bounce it meant to buy the dip of. GD is the clean illustration: 371.51 -> 375.305 -> 370.415 inside seventeen minutes, with the fill at 374.4437 catching 82% of the pop.
finding.why_it_survived: The existing rule 'never price a decision off the opening auction print' was written about MARKS, not FILLS. Re-quoting before deciding and then executing into the same window obeys the letter and collects the artifact anyway -- a check that passes for the wrong reason.
finding.fix: PREFER taking the day's autonomous equity entry on the first run at or after ~14:15Z, once the current session's report is on master. Nothing decays in 40 minutes on a 1-3 week hold off a day-old signal, and the same deferral also retires _REPORT_CRON_GAP_AT_THE_OPEN, because the run would then act on TODAY's report. Two defects, one change, no gate loosened. Written into CLAUDE.md this run.
finding.honest_scope: n=4, total measured cost ~$14 -- a refinement, not a crisis, and it must not be reported as one. Buying lower is not automatically better for mean reversion; what is notable is that the improvement existed in 4 of 4 cases. ROST filled mid-range (44.3%), so 'the run always buys the top' would be false, and GD's session is incomplete.

entries.finding_MECHANICAL_EXIT_HAS_NO_MAGNITUDE: THE HEADLINE: the mechanical take-profit's two gates -- RSI2>=70 and price>entry -- are NEAR-INDEPENDENT, so both can be true at a gain of a few cents. MEASURED on MDLZ: RSI2 crosses 70 at 62.7337, which is +0.230% from the 62.5899 entry = $1.15 gross on 7.988509 sh, against the position's own written target of 64.70 = $16.86. The clause would bank 6.8% of the trade's stated objective and consume a book slot doing it. || MECHANISM (the transferable part): RSI2 is a function of the recent PRICE PATH, P/L a function of the ENTRY LEVEL. The price at which the authority fires is set by one thing, the size of what it banks by another. A position entered at or near a local high -- exactly what a mean-reversion entry filled in the opening window tends to be, per the 13:52Z opening-window slippage finding -- satisfies both gates at a trivial gain. The worse the entry, the smaller the gain at which the exit fires: the clause pays least where execution was worst. || THIS IS THE MIRROR OF THE HOLE ALREADY FIXED, IN THE SAME SENTENCE. The 2026-08-26 correction added price>entry to stop the exit realizing a LOSS on a technical bounce (it fired on PNC at RSI2 78.5 while 0.34% underwater). That fix is right and stands -- but it bounds only the SIGN of the outcome, never its MAGNITUDE, and nobody checked the other end. This file's most-repeated shape: a rule written against one failure mode assumed to have bounded the whole quantity. || THE RULE: an RSI2>=70 print is a mechanical take-profit only when the gain is worth banking against the trade's OWN written target -- roughly a third of the entry-to-target distance as a working floor. Below that it is an OPTIONAL exit-into-strength needing a HARD RULE 7 thesis break or a graded rotation reason, never a technical trigger alone. Identical resolution to the 2026-08-26 underwater case, applied to the trivially-green one. No other gate changes. || HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, because it is not one-sided: selling MDLZ at 62.73 frees ~$501 and takes deployable from $302.10 to ~$803, which is the difference between a book that can enter and one that cannot. That is real. But it is a ROTATION argument, and rotation requires a GRADED incoming idea that beats the position sold. None exists this run. Freeing capital for an idea you have not had yet is selling on the hope of a signal. || HONEST SCOPE: it changed no decision -- MDLZ printed 66.07, not 70, so the authority was never armed. That is the only condition under which a filter's own thresholds can be audited credibly, the same standard the volume-baseline findings hold themselves to. n=1 name; the one-third fraction is a judgement, not a measured optimum. What is established firmly is the STRUCTURAL point: no bound on the gain follows from either gate. || DETECTOR, two lines of arithmetic off numbers already in the ledger: compute the gain at the trigger price and the gain at the written target. If the first is a small fraction of the second, the clause fired on its technical leg with its economic leg absent -- decline and say which.

finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.measured: GS read +0.622% against adjusted_previous_close 1020.90 -- which sits EXACTLY $5.00 below the raw previous_close 1025.90, i.e. GS went ex-dividend today. Against the raw close it is +0.132%, essentially flat. And XLF was +0.399% at the same timestamp, so on either measure GS LAGS its own sector rather than leading the cohort. The exception is an artifact twice over. LMT shows the same mechanic in the other direction: adjusted 557.78 vs raw 561.23 ($3.45, also ex-dividend), reading -0.489% adjusted against -1.101% raw. Two of twenty names carried an adjustment, so it is not a rare edge case.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.mechanism: A dividend adjustment shifts the denominator of the day-change calculation without any trade occurring, crediting the name with the dividend it just paid away. On a day when the whole cohort is red, an ex-dividend name is therefore the MOST LIKELY name to appear green -- precisely the name where greenness is least informative about whether buyers are present.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.detector: When the cohort yields exactly one green name, before working it: (a) compare adjusted_previous_close to previous_close on that name -- any gap is a corporate action, and the RAW figure is the one that says whether it actually traded up; (b) quote its sector ETF at the same timestamp and require the name to BEAT it, not merely to be green while the sector is green.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION. The entry was declined on the cohort distribution before the exception was examined, and would have been declined had GS been genuinely green -- one session of relative strength does not repair a weak setup, as the parent finding already states. Recorded because a filter's inputs can only be audited credibly on a run where the audit does not license a trade. n=1 green name on n=1 session: the MECHANISM is general, the magnitude is not.
finding_cohort_exception_needs_two_check.family: Same class as the affordability-tier bug (spot price / ATM strike / wrong expiry board), the four denominator modes, and the entry-day-bar error -- a number taken from a convenient field that was never quite the thing being asked about. First appearance in the EQUITY cohort screen rather than an options or volume input.

finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.headline: THE 2026-08-28 DIRECTION RULE IS CORRECT AND ITS PRESCRIBED SUBSTITUTION IS AN UNDERESTIMATE -- BECAUSE THE ONE DEFECTIVE MINUTE THAT CORRUPTS THE BUCKET IS ITSELF A TERM IN THE 1-MINUTE SUM YOU SUBSTITUTE. Measured 9.5-11%, in the dangerous direction.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.how_this_run_came_to_measure_it: The 15:00Z run flagged a 14:40Z hole on both indices, deliberately did NOT correct it (no volume baseline was load-bearing that run), and handed the reconciliation to whichever run first used the bucket. This run makes session-extreme claims that depend on it, so the debt was owed here. That handoff protocol worked exactly as designed and is worth keeping.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.reconciliation_performed: SPY 14:40Z bucket reported 2,280 against a 1-minute sum of 127,793 = -98.2%; QQQ reported 4,436 against 96,260 = -95.4%. Both are materially BELOW their sums, so per the 2026-08-28 direction rule the BUCKET is the holed side and the sum substitutes. Both reported volumes equal their 14:44 one-minute bar EXACTLY (2,280 and 4,436) -- the documented single-constituent signature -- and SPY's bucket OHLC is byte-for-byte its 14:44 minute (764.050/764.105/764.105/764.025). CONTROL in the same call: IWM's 14:40Z bucket reported 128,392 against a 128,336 sum = +0.04%, CLEAN.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_new_part: The 14:44 one-minute bar is ITSELF holed by this file's own recognition test -- a bar that is a tiny fraction of BOTH neighbours. SPY 14:44 = 2,280 = 12.9% of the prior minute (17,717) and 12.3% of the next (18,509); QQQ 14:44 = 4,436 = 30.8% / 30.0%. So the substituted 1-minute sum still carries the defective minute as one of its five terms. Imputing 14:44 at its neighbour mean gives a true bucket of ~143,626 (SPY) and ~106,422 (QQQ), against substituted floors of 127,793 and 96,260 -- the prescribed fix UNDERSTATES by 11.0% and 9.5%.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.why_it_matters_and_the_direction: It understates a VOLUME DENOMINATOR, which is the confirmation-manufacturing direction this file has now recorded four separate ways (session-average too strict, trailing-local too easy in a decaying tape, closing-auction too easy in absolute terms, holed-bucket too low). A trailing baseline built on the substituted sum is still ~10% light, so a candidate bar clears it ~10% too easily. The correction does not repair that; it BOUNDS it.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_mechanism_which_is_the_transferable_: The 5-minute bucket did not merely under-report -- it ADOPTED the defective minute wholesale, OHLC included. So the bad minute and the bad bucket are ONE defect observed at two resolutions, not two independent ones. That is why the direction rule works at all, and equally why its substitution cannot be exact: you are summing a series that contains the very corruption you are correcting for.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.the_rule_to_apply: Treat a direction-rule substitution as a FLOOR, and label it one. When the bucket's reported volume EXACTLY equals one constituent minute, check that minute against its own neighbours before summing; if it also carries the hole signature, impute it at the neighbour mean and state the result as a range (floor = raw sum, estimate = sum with the bad minute imputed). On a borderline confirmation call, use the imputed figure -- it is the conservative one, because a larger denominator makes confirmation harder.
finding_the_direction_rule_substitution_.honest_scope: THIS CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. No trigger was tested this run and no volume baseline was load-bearing. Both session-extreme claims survive the correction with room: SPY's true 14:40Z bucket high is 764.340, below the 764.549 session high set by the 14:35 bar; QQQ's is 710.2297, below the 711.090 set at 14:48. The imputation is an ESTIMATE from two neighbouring minutes, not a measurement -- the 9.5-11% figure is indicative, and n=2 symbols on one bucket. IWM's cleanliness in the identical window is read in ONE direction only, per the 2026-08-27 caveat: cross-symbol agreement evidences a hole, a clean third symbol evidences nothing.

The 2026-08-28 conclusion that hole offsets carry NO information is re-confirmed. Reconcile every window you intend to use; never skip on a positional prior.

finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.summary: The 14:35Z run measured an oversold cohort at 20 names, mean -1.97% vs SPY -0.40%, 1 of 20 green -- and found that single green name was an ex-dividend artifact AND lagging its own sector, concluding the cohort rule's exception clause needs TWO FREE CHECKS before it fires: (1) is the green a name-specific artifact, and (2) is the name leading or lagging its sector. This run applied that clause to a fresh case and it produced the OPPOSITE verdict. That is the useful result: a filter that has only ever vetoed is indistinguishable from a filter that always vetoes.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.the_case: LLY is the only one of the book's six equities green on the day: 1172.2782 against a 1156.73 prior close = +1.344%, while SPY is -0.475% and QQQ -0.985%. The tempting read, and the one this run started with, is that it is an ARTIFACT -- LLY fell 1.5% on Monday 08-31 on its own announced $2.88B acquisition of Merida Biosciences (MT Newswires 10:52 ET 08-31: 'Shares of Lilly were down 1.8%'), so today's green looks like a routine acquirer-side dip being bought back rather than relative strength.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.check_one_name_specific_artifact: FAILS TO DISQUALIFY. The deal-day dip retrace is real and is part of the move, but it is not the whole of it and it is not idiosyncratic noise: a 2.9-billion-dollar bolt-on is roughly 0.3% of LLY's market cap, an immaterial acquirer-side event, and the retrace of a 1.5% one-day drop cannot by itself be distinguished from ordinary mean reversion.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.check_two_leading_or_lagging_its_sector: FIRES AFFIRMATIVELY, and this is the check that settles it. Measured 15:24Z against prior closes: XLV +0.706% | ABBV +1.542% | LLY +1.344% | MRK +1.171% | JNJ +0.948% | AMGN +0.854% | PFE +0.615% | NVO +0.607% | BMY +0.389%. ALL NINE HEALTHCARE NAMES ARE GREEN and the sector ETF is up 0.71% against a -0.475% index. LLY is not a lone green print inside a red cohort at all -- it is participating in a broad defensive rotation, at roughly 1.9x its sector ETF, and it is not even the leader (ABBV is). The 14:35Z case and this one look identical from a single quote and are opposite once the sector is measured, which is precisely why the check is free and mandatory.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.verdict: NOT AN ARTIFACT. LLY's outperformance is genuine sector participation. The correct characterisation of the tape is therefore a DEFENSIVE ROTATION -- money into health care, out of the Nasdaq (-0.985%), with financials giving back the morning firmness four earlier runs carried (XLF +0.399% at 14:26Z, now -0.268%). Handing that forward as NUMBERS per the 2026-08-31 lesson, not as a frame.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.transferable_lesson: AN EXCEPTION CLAUSE THAT HAS ONLY EVER VETOED HAS NOT BEEN TESTED -- it has been ASSUMED. The 14:35Z clause was written from one case where both checks disqualified the green name, and a clause validated only by its own confirming instance is the same defect this file has now recorded repeatedly in the volume-baseline arc: a filter that rejects everything looks like discipline and looks like a bug from the same distance. The first case that makes it FIRE is worth more than the case that created it, because it is the only evidence the clause discriminates rather than merely refuses. Apply the same standard to the next filter written from a single instance.
finding_THE_GREEN_NAME_EXCEPTION_CLAUSE_.honest_scope: IT CHANGED NO DECISION, which is the only condition under which a filter's inputs can be audited credibly. LLY is underwater -1.47% against its 1189.7553 entry, so the profit-banking gate (price > entry) fails and no exit is available whatever the green means; and the equity book is capital-bound at $302.10 deployable, so no entry could act on a defensive-rotation read either. n=1 in the confirming direction does not make the clause reliable -- it makes it non-vacuous, which is a strictly weaker and still worth-having claim.

entries.finding: See holdings.json._A_ONE_DAY_MA_SLOPE_IS_NOT_A_FORWARD_PATH. Measured: QQQ 50-day one-day slope -0.4772/day implies the falling level reaches spot in 6.6 sessions and the bearish break self-repairs on a flat tape. Rolling the 50-close window with QQQ pinned at 708.450 gives 711.587 / 710.997 / 710.893 / 710.849 / 710.691 / 710.729 / 710.417 / 709.858 / 709.523 -- -0.258/day, and eight sessions out a motionless QQQ is still 1.07 BELOW its 50-day. The break PERSISTS. Mechanism: the one-day slope is a single 21.19-point close swap (737.95 out, 716.76 in) divided by 50 and says nothing about the next eight departures, which average 718.18 against the 708.450 replacing them. Same measurement as the 2026-08-25T19:00Z QQQ 20-day finding but with the OPPOSITE result, which is the point -- the slope's reliability is not predictable from the slope. Secondary correction: the 20d/50d convergence is ~-0.41/day rolled, not the -1.311/day the naive rates imply, so a cross is nearer 17 sessions than 5.5. HONEST SCOPE: changed no decision -- the QQQ trigger was already declined twice, on the 16:20Z volume clause and on capital.

entries.union_merge_bug_caught: MEASURED WHILE PERFORMING THIS UNION, and it is a defect in HOW a union is done rather than in any run's trading: a first attempt de-duplicated on the key (run_utc, headline[:80]) and produced 812 entries where the correct union is 816. FOUR distinct historical entries -- 2026-08-13T18:30Z, 2026-08-13T23:29Z, 2026-08-14T17:15Z, 2026-08-14T19:15Z -- predate the `headline` field, so their key collapsed to (timestamp, empty string) and the second of each pair was silently dropped. The union protocol says keep BOTH entries; a dedup key built from a field that is not universal quietly violates it. THE RULE: when unioning trade_journal.json, de-duplicate on EXACT serialized content (json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True)) and NEVER on a composite of chosen fields, then ASSERT the expected count (len(shared) + one entry per colliding run) before writing. Same shape as the git diff --stat rule and the lot-invariant assertion: trust the check, not your reading of the merge.

entries.finding: _EXTENDED_IS_NOT_LESS_LIKELY_TO_REACH_TARGET_THAN_OVERSOLD written to holdings.json. The 17:15Z rotation decline recorded its own honest weakness -- that comparing ROST's REMAINING upside to a candidate's TOTAL upside treats two unequal probabilities as equal, because RSI2 83.2 is extended. Measured on ROST's own 752 daily bars (2023-09-01..2026-09-01), Wilder RSI2 validated by reproducing the desk's independently-measured 35.547 settled reading to three decimals: over 15 sessions the EXTENDED (RSI2>=80) cohort reaches +5.19% intrabar 38.0% of the time against the OVERSOLD (RSI2<10) cohort's 39.8%, with the extended cohort carrying the higher mean (+1.20% vs +0.92%), median (+1.85% vs -0.02%) and positive rate (60.6% vs 49.4%). The asserted asymmetry is not visible in this name's data, so it cannot carry the rotation either way -- and the 17:15Z decline was, if anything, conservative. Second and less comfortable result: the OVERSOLD cohort's median 15-session return is -0.02%, i.e. the entry trigger's edge on this name is a RIGHT-TAIL edge rather than a central-tendency one, which independently supports the magnitude floor from a direction its own derivation never used. Honest scope stated in the key: one name, in-sample on the position being decided, heavily overlapping observations, no significance claimed.

entries.findings: TWO durable keys written to holdings.json. (1) _A_SECTOR_DE_RATE_HIDES_INSIDE_A_NEWSLESS_SINGLE_NAME -- this file's rule ranks a newsless decline as the WEAKER veto, and at the single-name level UNP qualifies; that reading is wrong when the peers moved with it. ALWAYS QUOTE THE PEERS BEFORE CALLING A DECLINE NEWSLESS: one name wandering without a cause is probably noise, three correlated names moving 4.5-5.5% on 1.2-2.4x volume is a cause not yet identified, and the single-name feed is exactly where a sector de-rate is invisible. (2) _SETTLE_MECHANICAL_EXITS_BEFORE_COMPUTING_THE_CAPITAL_GATE -- the rotation gate was disposing of the whole screen on the premise that funding requires a rotation sell, while ROST held a live authorized mechanical exit that would supply funding with none. Correct sequence: settle authorized mechanical exits on their own merits FIRST, then compute the capital gate on the resulting cash, then apply the rotation gate only if deployable is still short. Grading a screen against a capital number an unexercised exit authority can change is a stale denominator. Tested in the correct order today and it changed nothing -- which is the only condition under which a process audit is credible -- but it would flip the answer on a day with an A-grade name.

entries.why_this_advances_the_open_question: The 18:20Z run put a BINARY to Ryan -- target-based vs Connors-pure -- having measured both unsatisfying (targets ~6% away and rarely reached; the RSI2>=70 cross sits a mean 0.84% from entry BY CONSTRUCTION and banks ~0-1%). A time stop is immune to that specific defect because it is indexed on elapsed time rather than on the same price range the entry came from. But the honest reading is SUPERSESSION, not a forgotten feature: CLAUDE.md's monthly-rebalance cull ALREADY IS the swing time stop, at ~30 days instead of 14. That shrinks the question for Ryan from 'which of two exit systems' to a cadence choice, and the recommendation is to DELETE the constant rather than wire it -- a third automatic time-based exit would add a third disagreeing system to a book already deadlocked between two.
entries.the_hazard_recorded_as_a_class: Dead code that reads as live policy is worse than no code: a future run grepping the exit block finds a named constant, in the exit-thresholds block, between two enforced ones, with an authoritative comment, and has every reason to believe swings carry a 14-day time stop. Nothing errors; the belief is simply false. This file's most-repeated defect -- a check that passes for the wrong reason -- arriving as a CONSTANT that looks enforced.

entries.finding: _TIME_STOP_NEEDS_NO_REPORT_BUT_THE_RSI2_EXIT_NEEDS_A_LIVE_ONE (new, in holdings.json). Named here, not re-argued. Two halves: (a) report.py's TIME STOP branch reads only sleeve, entry_date and today -- no price, no rsi2, no ma200 -- so it is pure ledger arithmetic and a stale report cannot gate it; it is also the book's only mechanical loss discipline and prompt v10 never throttles a mechanical exit. (b) the RSI2>=70 branch DOES read a live technical, and the connector's RSI2 is not interchangeable with the report's: measured on the same 2026-09-02 close, MMM 1.1 vs 0.8236 and GD 1.9 vs 1.9442 (agree to <0.3) but ROST 83.2 vs 73.1276 (10.07 apart). The agreement is good at the oversold extreme because a 2-period RSI pinned by two down closes collapses to ~0 under any smoothing, and poor in the upper range where up and down closes mix -- so the ENTRY screen sits where the sources agree and the EXIT trigger sits where they do not.
